5.6.m: those who discharge feces and the like in cowpens, fires, waters, streets, / in the shade of trees, on mountains, and in pleasure gardens and shrines;

5.6.s:
lajjāśramaprāsādeṣu madyapānaratāśca ye |
kṛtakelibhujaṅgāśca randhrānveṣaṇatatparāḥ ||
5.6.d:
लज्जाश्रमप्रासादेषु मद्यपानरताश्च ये ।
कृतकेलिभुजङ्गाश्च रन्ध्रान्वेषणतत्पराः ॥
5.6.m: those who indulge in wine drinking in modest homes, hermitages, and palaces; / debauchees skilled in games, and those intent on seeking the faults of others;

5.6.s:
vaṃśeṣṭakāśilākāṣṭhaiḥ śṛṅgaiḥ śaṅkubhireva ca |
ye mārgamanurundhanti parasīmāṃ haranti ye ||
5.6.d:
वंशेष्टकाशिलाकाष्ठैः शृङ्गैः शङ्कुभिरेव च ।
ये मार्गमनुरुन्धन्ति परसीमां हरन्ति ये ॥
5.6.m: those who obstruct a path with bamboo, bricks, stones, wood, / horns, and stakes, and those who seize another's boundary;

5.6.s:
kūṭaśāsanakartāraḥ kūṭakarmakriyāratāḥ |
kūṭapākānnavastrāṇāṃ kūṭasaṃvyavahāriṇaḥ ||
5.6.d:
कूटशासनकर्तारः कूटकर्मक्रियारताः ।
कूटपाकान्नवस्त्राणां कूटसंव्यवहारिणः ॥
5.6.m: forgers of royal decrees, those intent on performing fraudulent deeds, / and dishonest dealers in counterfeit cooked food, grain, and cloth;

5.6.s:
dhanuṣaḥ śastraśalyānāṃ kartā yaḥ krayavikrayī |
nirdayo'tīva bhṛtyeṣu paśūnāṃ damanaśca yaḥ ||
5.6.d:
धनुषः शस्त्रशल्यानां कर्ता यः क्रयविक्रयी ।
निर्दयोऽतीव भृत्येषु पशूनां दमनश्च यः ॥
5.6.m: one who makes or buys and sells bows, weapons, and iron points; / one who is exceedingly merciless toward servants, and one who torments animals;

5.6.s:
mithyā pravadato vāca ākarṇayati yaḥ śanaiḥ |
svāmimitragurudrohī māyāvī capalaḥ śaṭhaḥ ||
5.6.d:
मिथ्या प्रवदतो वाच आकर्णयति यः शनैः ।
स्वामिमित्रगुरुद्रोही मायावी चपलः शठः ॥
5.6.m: he who secretly listens to the words of someone speaking falsehood; / one who betrays master, friend, or guru, deceitful, fickle, and roguish;

5.6.s:
ye bhāryāputramitrāṇi bālavṛddhakṛśāturān |
bhṛtyānatithibandhūṃśca tyaktvāśnanti bubhukṣitān ||
5.6.d:
ये भार्यापुत्रमित्राणि बालवृद्धकृशातुरान् ।
भृत्यानतिथिबन्धूंश्च त्यक्त्वाश्नन्ति बुभुक्षितान् ॥
5.6.m: those who eat leaving their wives, sons, friends, children, / the elderly, the emaciated, the sick, their servants, guests, and relatives hungry;

5.6.s:
yaḥ svayaṃ miṣṭamaśnāti viprebhyo na prayacchati |
vṛthāpākaḥ sa vijñeyo brahmavādiṣu garhitaḥ ||
5.6.d:
यः स्वयं मिष्टमश्नाति विप्रेभ्यो न प्रयच्छति ।
वृथापाकः स विज्ञेयो ब्रह्मवादिषु गर्हितः ॥
5.6.m: he who eats sweets himself and does not give them to Brahmins, / is to be known as one who cooks in vain, condemned among the expounders of the Veda;

5.6.s:
niyamān svayamādāya ye tyajantyajitendriyāḥ |
pravrajyāvāsitā ye ca harasyāsyaprabhedakāḥ ||
5.6.d:
नियमान् स्वयमादाय ये त्यजन्त्यजितेन्द्रियाः ।
प्रव्रज्यावासिता ये च हरस्यास्यप्रभेदकाः ॥
5.6.m: those of uncontrolled senses who, having themselves undertaken vows, abandon them; / those settled in monastic life [yet fall away], and those who cause dissension in Hara's assembly;

5.6.s:
ye tāḍayanti gāṃ krūrā damayante muhurmuhuḥ |
durbalānye na puṣṇanti satataṃ ye tyajanti ca ||
5.6.d:
ये ताडयन्ति गां क्रूरा दमयन्ते मुहुर्मुहुः ।
दुर्बलान्ये न पुष्णन्ति सततं ये त्यजन्ति च ॥
5.6.m: those cruel people who strike a cow and repeatedly torment it, / who do not nourish the weak, and who constantly abandon them;

5.6.s:
pīḍayantyatibhāreṇāsahantaṃ vāhayanti ca |
yojayantyakṛtāhārānna vimuñcanti saṃyatān ||
5.6.d:
पीडयन्त्यतिभारेणासहन्तं वाहयन्ति च ।
योजयन्त्यकृताहारान्न विमुञ्चन्ति संयतान् ॥
5.6.m: who afflict it with excessive burdens and make it pull when it cannot endure, / who yoke them without feeding them, and do not untie them when bound;

5.6.s:
ye bhārakṣatarogārtān govṛṣāṃśca kṣudhāturān |
na pālayanti yatnena goghnāste nārakāḥ smṛtāḥ ||
5.6.d:
ये भारक्षतरोगार्तान् गोवृषांश्च क्षुधातुरान् ।
न पालयन्ति यत्नेन गोघ्नास्ते नारकाः स्मृताः ॥
5.6.m: those who do not carefully care for cows and bulls afflicted by heavy loads, wounds, disease, / and hunger—they are considered cow-killers, destined for hell.

5.6.s:
vṛṣāṇāṃ vṛṣaṇānye ca pāpiṣṭhā gālayanti ca |
vāhayanti ca gāṃ vandhyāṃ mahānārakino narāḥ ||
5.6.d:
वृषाणां वृषणान्ये च पापिष्ठा गालयन्ति च ।
वाहयन्ति च गां वन्ध्यां महानारकिनो नराः ॥
5.6.m: And those most sinful men who castrate bulls / and yoke a barren cow are destined for great hell.

5.6.s:
āśayā samanuprāptān kṣuttṛṣṇāśramakarśitān |
atithīṃśca tathānāthān svatantrān gṛhamāgatān ||
5.6.d:
आशया समनुप्राप्तान् क्षुत्तृष्णाश्रमकर्शितान् ।
अतिथींश्च तथानाथान् स्वतन्त्रान् गृहमागतान् ॥
5.6.m: Those who, arrived with hope, worn out by hunger, thirst, and fatigue, / guests, the helpless, or independent [travelers] who have come to the house,

5.6.s:
annābhilāṣān dīnānvā bālavṛddhakṛśāturān |
nānukampanti ye mūḍhāste yānti narakārṇavam ||
5.6.d:
अन्नाभिलाषान् दीनान्वा बालवृद्धकृशातुरान् ।
नानुकम्पन्ति ये मूढास्ते यान्ति नरकार्णवम् ॥
5.6.m: desiring food, or wretched, the young, the old, the emaciated, and the sick— / the fools who have no pity for these go to the ocean of hell.

5.6.s:
gṛheṣvarthā nivartante śmaśānādapi bāndhavāḥ |
sukṛtaṃ duṣkṛtaṃ caiva gacchantamanugacchati ||
5.6.d:
गृहेष्वर्था निवर्तन्ते श्मशानादपि बान्धवाः ।
सुकृतं दुष्कृतं चैव गच्छन्तमनुगच्छति ॥
5.6.m: Wealth stays behind in houses; relatives turn back even from the cremation ground; / both good deed and bad deed follow the one who departs.

5.6.s:
ajāviko māhiṣikaḥ sāmudro vṛṣalīpatiḥ |
śūdravatkṣatravṛttiśca nārakī syād dvijādhamaḥ ||
5.6.d:
अजाविको माहिषिकः सामुद्रो वृषलीपतिः ।
शूद्रवत्क्षत्रवृत्तिश्च नारकी स्याद् द्विजाधमः ॥
5.6.m: A breeder of goats and sheep, a buffalo-keeper, a sea-trader, the husband of a Śūdra woman, / and one who adopts the livelihood of a Kṣatriya like a Śūdra: such a degraded twice-born goes to hell.

5.6.s:
śilpinaḥ kāravo vaidyā hemakārā nṛpadhvajāḥ |
bhṛtakāḥ kūṭasaṃyuktāḥ sarve te nārakāḥ smṛtāḥ ||
5.6.d:
शिल्पिनः कारवो वैद्या हेमकारा नृपध्वजाः ।
भृतकाः कूटसंयुक्ताः सर्वे ते नारकाः स्मृताः ॥
5.6.m: Artisans, craftsmen, physicians, goldsmiths, royal heralds, / and deceitful servants—all these are traditionally regarded as destined for hell.

5.6.s:
yaścocitamatikramya svecchayaivāharetkaram |
narake pacyate so'pi yo'pi daṇḍarucirnaraḥ ||
5.6.d:
यश्चोचितमतिक्रम्य स्वेच्छयैवाहरेत्करम् ।
नरके पच्यते सोऽपि योऽपि दण्डरुचिर्नरः ॥
5.6.m: And whoever exceeds what is fitting and collects a tax merely by his own whim, / that man is boiled in hell, as is one who delights in punishment.

5.6.s:
utkocakai rucikrītaistaskaraiśca prapīḍyate |
yasya rājñaḥ prajā rāṣṭre pacyate narakeṣu saḥ ||
5.6.d:
उत्कोचकै रुचिक्रीतैस्तस्करैश्च प्रपीड्यते ।
यस्य राज्ञः प्रजा राष्ट्रे पच्यते नरकेषु सः ॥
5.6.m: A king in whose realm the subjects are oppressed by bribe-takers, / by those bought by desire, and by thieves, is boiled in the hells.

5.6.s:
ye dvijāḥ parigṛhṇanti nṛpasyānyāyavartinaḥ |
te prayānti tu ghoreṣu narakeṣu na saṃśayaḥ ||
5.6.d:
ये द्विजाः परिगृह्णन्ति नृपस्यान्यायवर्तिनः ।
ते प्रयान्ति तु घोरेषु नरकेषु न संशयः ॥
5.6.m: The twice-born who accept [gifts] from a king behaving unjustly / proceed indeed into terrifying hells; there is no doubt.

5.6.s:
anyāyātsamupādāya dvijebhyo yaḥ prayacchati |
prajābhyaḥ pacyate so'pi narakeṣu nṛpo yathā ||
5.6.d:
अन्यायात्समुपादाय द्विजेभ्यो यः प्रयच्छति ।
प्रजाभ्यः पच्यते सोऽपि नरकेषु नृपो यथा ॥
5.6.m: He who takes unjustly from his subjects / and gives to the twice-born is also boiled in the hells, just like that king.

5.6.s:
pāradārikacaurāṇāṃ caṇḍānāṃ vidyate tvagham |
paradāraratasyāpi rājño bhavati nityaśaḥ ||
5.6.d:
पारदारिकचौराणां चण्डानां विद्यते त्वघम् ।
परदाररतस्यापि राज्ञो भवति नित्यशः ॥
5.6.m: The sin belonging to adulterers, thieves, and violent men / falls constantly upon a king who is also devoted to another's wife.

5.6.s:
acauraṃ cauravatpaśyeccauraṃ vācaurarūpiṇam |
avicārya nṛpastasmād ghātayannarakaṃ vrajet ||
5.6.d:
अचौरं चौरवत्पश्येच्चौरं वाचौररूपिणम् ।
अविचार्य नृपस्तस्माद् घातयन्नरकं व्रजेत् ॥
5.6.m: A king who views an innocent person as a thief or a thief as an innocent person, / and slays [them] without inquiry, would go to hell.

5.6.s:
ghṛtatailānnapānāni madhumāṃsasurāsavam |
guḍekṣuśākadugdhāni dadhimūlaphalāni ca ||
5.6.d:
घृततैलान्नपानानि मधुमांससुरासवम् ।
गुडेक्षुशाकदुग्धानि दधिमूलफलानि च ॥
5.6.m: Ghee, oil, food, drinks, honey, meat, spirituous liquor, and wine, / molasses, sugarcane, vegetables, milk, curds, roots, and fruits,

5.6.s:
tṛṇaṃ kāṣṭhaṃ patrapuṣpamauṣadhaṃ cātmabhojanam |
upānatchatraśakaṭamāsanaṃ ca kamaṇḍalum ||
5.6.d:
तृणं काष्ठं पत्रपुष्पमौषधं चात्मभोजनम् ।
उपानत्छत्रशकटमासनं च कमण्डलुम् ॥
5.6.m: grass, wood, leaves, flowers, medicine, one’s own food, / sandals, an umbrella, a cart, a seat, and a water-pot,

5.6.s:
tāmrasīsatrapuḥ śastraṃ śaṅkhādyaṃ ca jalodbhavam |
vādyaṃ ca vaiṇavaṃ cānyadgṛhopaskaraṇāni ca ||
5.6.d:
ताम्रसीसत्रपुः शस्त्रं शङ्खाद्यं च जलोद्भवम् ।
वाद्यं च वैणवं चान्यद्गृहोपस्करणानि च ॥
5.6.m: copper, lead, tin, a weapon, conch-shells and other things born of water, / musical instruments, flutes, and other household utensils,

5.6.s:
aurṇṇakārpāsakauśeyapaṭṭasūtrodbhavāni ca |
sthūlasūkṣmāṇi vastrāṇi ye lobhāddhi haranti ca ||
5.6.d:
और्ण्णकार्पासकौशेयपट्टसूत्रोद्भवानि च ।
स्थूलसूक्ष्माणि वस्त्राणि ये लोभाद्धि हरन्ति च ॥
5.6.m: and coarse or fine garments made of wool, / cotton, silk, and woven threads—those who steal these out of greed,

5.6.s:
evamādīni cānyāni dravyāṇi vividhāni ca |
narakeṣu dhruvaṃ yānti cāpahṛtyālpakāni ca ||
5.6.d:
एवमादीनि चान्यानि द्रव्याणि विविधानि च ।
नरकेषु ध्रुवं यान्ति चापहृत्याल्पकानि च ॥
5.6.m: and other diverse goods of this kind, / even if stealing small amounts, certainly go to the hells.

5.6.s:
tadvā yadvā paradravyamapi sarṣapamātrakam |
apahṛtya narā yānti narakaṃ nātra saṃśayaḥ ||
5.6.d:
तद्वा यद्वा परद्रव्यमपि सर्षपमात्रकम् ।
अपहृत्य नरा यान्ति नरकं नात्र संशयः ॥
5.6.m: Stealing another's property, whether that or whatever else, / even to the measure of a mustard seed, men go to hell; there is no doubt here.

5.6.s:
evamādyairnaraḥ pāpairutkrāntisamanantaram |
śarīrayātanārthāya sarvākāramavāpnuyāt ||
5.6.d:
एवमाद्यैर्नरः पापैरुत्क्रान्तिसमनन्तरम् ।
शरीरयातनार्थाय सर्वाकारमवाप्नुयात् ॥
5.6.m: Immediately after departing [this life] through such sins, / a man obtains a [new] body of every form for the purpose of enduring torment.

5.6.s:
yamalokaṃ vrajantyete śarīreṇa yamājñayā |
yamadūtairmahāghorairnīyamānāḥ suduḥkhitāḥ ||
5.6.d:
यमलोकं व्रजन्त्येते शरीरेण यमाज्ञया ।
यमदूतैर्महाघोरैर्नीयमानाः सुदुःखिताः ॥
5.6.m: Led by the terrifying messengers of Yama by Yama's command, / these go to the world of Yama with that body, intensely suffering.

5.6.s:
devatiryaṅmanuṣyāṇāmadharmaniratātmanām |
dharmarājaḥ smṛtaḥ śāstā sughorairvividhairvadhaiḥ ||
5.6.d:
देवतिर्यङ्मनुष्याणामधर्मनिरतात्मनाम् ।
धर्मराजः स्मृतः शास्ता सुघोरैर्विविधैर्वधैः ॥
5.6.m: Dharmarāja is remembered as the punisher of gods, animals, and humans / whose minds are devoted to unrighteousness, with dreadful, diverse executions.

5.6.s:
niyamācārayuktānāṃ pramādātskhalitātmanām |
prāyaścittairguruḥ śāstā na budhairiṣyate yamaḥ ||
5.6.d:
नियमाचारयुक्तानां प्रमादात्स्खलितात्मनाम् ।
प्रायश्चित्तैर्गुरुः शास्ता न बुधैरिष्यते यमः ॥
5.6.m: For those endowed with observances and conduct whose minds slip through negligence, / the guru is the punisher through expiations; Yama is not desired by the wise [for them].

5.6.s:
pāradārikacaurāṇāmanyāyavyavahāriṇām |
nṛpatiḥ śāsakaḥ proktaḥ pracchannānāṃ sa dharmmarāṭ ||
5.6.d:
पारदारिकचौराणामन्यायव्यवहारिणाम् ।
नृपतिः शासकः प्रोक्तः प्रच्छन्नानां स धर्म्मराट् ॥
5.6.m: The king is declared the punisher of adulterers, thieves, / and those who deal unjustly; of the secret [sinners], that King of Dharma [Yama is the punisher].

5.6.s:
tasmāt kṛtasya pāpasya prāyaścittaṃ samācaret |
nābhuktasyānyathā nāśaḥ kalpakoṭiśatairapi ||
5.6.d:
तस्मात् कृतस्य पापस्य प्रायश्चित्तं समाचरेत् ।
नाभुक्तस्यान्यथा नाशः कल्पकोटिशतैरपि ॥
5.6.m: Therefore, one should perform expiation for a committed sin; / otherwise, what is unexperienced does not perish even in hundreds of millions of kalpas.

5.6.s:
yaḥ karoti svayaṃ karma kārayeccānumodayet |
kāyena manasā vācā tasya pāpagatiḥ phalam ||
śrīgaṇeśāya namaḥ ||
śrīgaurīśaṅkarābhyāṃ namaḥ ||
śrīśivamahāpurāṇam ||
5.6.d:
यः करोति स्वयं कर्म कारयेच्चानुमोदयेत् ।
कायेन मनसा वाचा तस्य पापगतिः फलम् ॥
श्रीगणेशाय नमः ॥
श्रीगौरीशङ्कराभ्यां नमः ॥
श्रीशिवमहापुराणम् ॥
5.6.m:
He who commits an act himself, causes it to be done, or approves it / with body, mind, or speech—his fruit is a sinful destination.

Homage to the holy Gaurī and Śaṅkara.

5.7.s:
sanatkumāra uvāca |
atha pāpairnarā yānti yamalokaṃ caturvidhaiḥ |
santrāsajananaṃ ghoraṃ vivaśāḥ sarvadehinaḥ ||
5.7.d:
सनत्कुमार उवाच ।
अथ पापैर्नरा यान्ति यमलोकं चतुर्विधैः ।
सन्त्रासजननं घोरं विवशाः सर्वदेहिनः ॥
5.7.m: Sanatkumāra said: / Now, through the four kinds of sins, all embodied beings go, / helpless, to the terrifying world of Yama that causes terror.

5.7.s:
garbhasthairjāyamānaiśca bālaistaruṇamadhyamaiḥ |
strīpunnapuṃsakairjīvairjñātavyaṃ sarvajantuṣu ||
5.7.d:
गर्भस्थैर्जायमानैश्च बालैस्तरुणमध्यमैः ।
स्त्रीपुन्नपुंसकैर्जीवैर्ज्ञातव्यं सर्वजन्तुषु ॥
5.7.m: This is to be understood among all creatures, by souls / in the womb, being born, children, youths, the middle-aged, women, men, and neuters.

5.7.s:
śubhāśubhaphalaṃ cātra dehināṃ saṃvicāryate |
citraguptādibhiḥ sarvaiḥ vasiṣṭhapramukhaistathā ||
5.7.d:
शुभाशुभफलं चात्र देहिनां संविचार्यते ।
चित्रगुप्तादिभिः सर्वैः वसिष्ठप्रमुखैस्तथा ॥
5.7.m: And here the fruit of good and evil deeds of embodied beings / is investigated by all, beginning with Citragupta, and by Vasiṣṭha and others.

5.7.s:
na kecitprāṇinaḥ santi ye na yānti yamakṣayam |
avaśyaṃ hi kṛtaṃ karma bhoktavyaṃ tadvicāryatām ||
5.7.d:
न केचित्प्राणिनः सन्ति ये न यान्ति यमक्षयम् ।
अवश्यं हि कृतं कर्म भोक्तव्यं तद्विचार्यताम् ॥
5.7.m: There are no living beings who do not go to the abode of Yama; / an action that has been done must inevitably be experienced: let that be reflected upon.

5.7.s:
tatra ye śubhakarmāṇaḥ saumyacittā dayānvitāḥ |
te narā yānti saumyena pūrvaṃ yamaniketanam ||
5.7.d:
तत्र ये शुभकर्माणः सौम्यचित्ता दयान्विताः ।
ते नरा यान्ति सौम्येन पूर्वं यमनिकेतनम् ॥
5.7.m: There, those whose deeds are auspicious, gentle-minded and full of compassion, / those men go by a gentle eastern [path] to Yama's dwelling.

5.7.s:
ye punaḥ pāpakarmāṇaḥ pāpā dānavivarjitāḥ |
te ghoreṇa pathā yānti dakṣiṇena yamālayam ||
5.7.d:
ये पुनः पापकर्माणः पापा दानविवर्जिताः ।
ते घोरेण पथा यान्ति दक्षिणेन यमालयम् ॥
5.7.m: On the other hand, those whose deeds are sinful, evil and devoid of charity, / go by a dreadful southern path to the abode of Yama.

5.7.s:
ṣaḍaśītisahasrāṇi yojanānāmatītya tat |
vaivasvatapuraṃ jñeyaṃ nānārūpamavasthitam ||
5.7.d:
षडशीतिसहस्राणि योजनानामतीत्य तत् ।
वैवस्वतपुरं ज्ञेयं नानारूपमवस्थितम् ॥
5.7.m: Eighty-six thousand yojanas away, / that city of Vaivasvata is to be known, established in various forms.

5.7.s:
samīpasthamivābhāti narāṇāṃ puṇyakarmaṇām |
pāpināmatidūrasthaṃ yathā raudreṇa gacchatām ||
5.7.d:
समीपस्थमिवाभाति नराणां पुण्यकर्मणाम् ।
पापिनामतिदूरस्थं यथा रौद्रेण गच्छताम् ॥
5.7.m: It appears as if nearby to men of meritorious deeds; / to sinners, as they go by the terrible [path], it lies exceedingly far away:

5.7.s:
tīkṣṇakaṇṭakayuktena śarkarāvicitena ca |
kṣuradhārānibhaistīkṣṇaiḥ pāṣāṇai racitena ca ||
5.7.d:
तीक्ष्णकण्टकयुक्तेन शर्कराविचितेन च ।
क्षुरधारानिभैस्तीक्ष्णैः पाषाणै रचितेन च ॥
5.7.m: [a path] set with sharp thorns and scattered with gravel, / and fashioned with sharp stones resembling razor blades;

5.7.s:
kvacitpaṅkena mahatā jalaukābhiśca saṅkulaiḥ |
lohasūcīnibhairdarbhaiḥ sampannena pathā kvacit ||
5.7.d:
क्वचित्पङ्केन महता जलौकाभिश्च सङ्कुलैः ।
लोहसूचीनिभैर्दर्भैः सम्पन्नेन पथा क्वचित् ॥
5.7.m: a path filled in some places with great mud and teeming with leeches, / and in some places provided with darbha grass resembling iron needles;

5.7.s:
taṭaprāyātiviṣamaiḥ parvatairvṛkṣasaṅkulaiḥ |
prataptāṅgārayuktena yānti mārgeṇa duḥkhitāḥ ||
5.7.d:
तटप्रायातिविषमैः पर्वतैर्वृक्षसङ्कुलैः ।
प्रतप्ताङ्गारयुक्तेन यान्ति मार्गेण दुःखिताः ॥
5.7.m: by a path exceedingly rugged with cliffs, mountains thick with trees, / and filled with glowing coals, the suffering ones go;

5.7.s:
kvacidviṣamagartaiśca kvacilloṣṭhaiḥ suduṣkaraiḥ |
sutaptabālukābhiśca tathā tīkṣṇaiśca śaṅkubhiḥ ||
5.7.d:
क्वचिद्विषमगर्तैश्च क्वचिल्लोष्ठैः सुदुष्करैः ।
सुतप्तबालुकाभिश्च तथा तीक्ष्णैश्च शङ्कुभिः ॥
5.7.m: in some places with rugged pits, and in some places with impassable clods of earth, / with scorching sands, and likewise with sharp stakes;

5.7.s:
anekaśākhāvitatairvyāptaṃ vaṃśavanaiḥ kvacit |
kaṣṭena tamasā mārgeṇānālambena kutracit ||
5.7.d:
अनेकशाखाविततैर्व्याप्तं वंशवनैः क्वचित् ।
कष्टेन तमसा मार्गेणानालम्बेन कुत्रचित् ॥
5.7.m: in some places covered with bamboo forests spreading many branches; / in some places by a difficult, dark path, without any support;

5.7.s:
ayaḥ śṛṅgāṭakaistīkṣṇaiḥ kvaciddāvāgninā punaḥ |
kvacittaptaśilābhiśca kvacidvyāptaṃ himena ca ||
5.7.d:
अयः शृङ्गाटकैस्तीक्ष्णैः क्वचिद्दावाग्निना पुनः ।
क्वचित्तप्तशिलाभिश्च क्वचिद्व्याप्तं हिमेन च ॥
5.7.m: again with sharp iron caltrops, in some places with a forest fire, / in some places with scorching rocks, and in some places covered with snow;

5.7.s:
kvacidvālukayā vyāptamākaṇṭhāntaḥ praveśayā |
kvacidduṣṭāmbunā vyāptaṃ kvacicca kariṣāgninā ||
5.7.d:
क्वचिद्वालुकया व्याप्तमाकण्ठान्तः प्रवेशया ।
क्वचिद्दुष्टाम्बुना व्याप्तं क्वचिच्च करिषाग्निना ॥
5.7.m: in some places covered with sand that sinks in up to the neck, / in some places covered with foul water, and in some places with fire fed by dried dung;

5.7.s:
kvacit sihairvṛkairvyāghrairmaśakaiśca sudāruṇaiḥ |
kvacinmahājalaukābhiḥ kvaciccājagaraistathā ||
5.7.d:
क्वचित् सिहैर्वृकैर्व्याघ्रैर्मशकैश्च सुदारुणैः ।
क्वचिन्महाजलौकाभिः क्वचिच्चाजगरैस्तथा ॥
5.7.m: in some places with lions, wolves, tigers, and dreadfully fierce mosquitoes, / in some places with giant leeches, and in some places with pythons;

5.7.s:
makṣikābhiśca raudrābhiḥ kvacit sarpairviṣolbaṇaiḥ |
mattamātaṅgayūthaiśca balonmattaiḥ pramāthibhiḥ ||
5.7.d:
मक्षिकाभिश्च रौद्राभिः क्वचित् सर्पैर्विषोल्बणैः ।
मत्तमातङ्गयूथैश्च बलोन्मत्तैः प्रमाथिभिः ॥
5.7.m: and with terrible flies, in some places with serpents swollen with poison, / and with herds of rutting elephants, maddened by strength and destructive;

5.7.s:
panthānamullikhadbhiśca sūkaraistīkṣṇadaṃṣṭribhiḥ |
tīkṣṇaśṛṅgaiśca mahiṣaiḥ sarvabhūtaiśca śvāpadaiḥ ||
5.7.d:
पन्थानमुल्लिखद्भिश्च सूकरैस्तीक्ष्णदंष्ट्रिभिः ।
तीक्ष्णशृङ्गैश्च महिषैः सर्वभूतैश्च श्वापदैः ॥
5.7.m: with sharp-tusked boars scraping the path, / and with sharp-horned buffaloes, and wild beasts of all kinds;

5.7.s:
ḍākinībhiśca raudrābhirvikarālaiśca rākṣasaiḥ |
vyādhibhiśca mahāghoraiḥ pīḍyamānā vrajanti hi ||
5.7.d:
डाकिनीभिश्च रौद्राभिर्विकरालैश्च राक्षसैः ।
व्याधिभिश्च महाघोरैः पीड्यमाना व्रजन्ति हि ॥
5.7.m: and with terrible ḍākinīs, hideous rākṣasas, / and most dreadful diseases—afflicted [by these], they go;

5.7.s:
mahādhūlivimiśreṇa mahācaṇḍena vāyunā |
mahāpāṣāṇavarṣeṇa hanyamānā nirāśrayāḥ ||
5.7.d:
महाधूलिविमिश्रेण महाचण्डेन वायुना ।
महापाषाणवर्षेण हन्यमाना निराश्रयाः ॥
5.7.m: struck, shelterless, by a fierce hurricane / mixed with thick dust, and by a rain of great stones;

5.7.s:
kvacidvidyutprapātena dahyamānā vrajanti ca |
mahatā bāṇavarṣeṇa vidhyamānāśca sarvataḥ ||
5.7.d:
क्वचिद्विद्युत्प्रपातेन दह्यमाना व्रजन्ति च ।
महता बाणवर्षेण विध्यमानाश्च सर्वतः ॥
5.7.m: and they go being burned in some places by flashes of lightning, / and pierced on all sides by a great shower of arrows;

5.7.s:
patadbhirvajrapātaiśca ulkāpātaiśca dāruṇaiḥ |
pradīptāṅgāravarṣeṇa dahyamānāśca santi hi ||
5.7.d:
पतद्भिर्वज्रपातैश्च उल्कापातैश्च दारुणैः ।
प्रदीप्ताङ्गारवर्षेण दह्यमानाश्च सन्ति हि ॥
5.7.m: and they are burned by falling thunderbolts, / by dreadful falls of meteors, and by a shower of blazing coals.

5.7.s:
mahatā pāṃsuvarṣeṇa pūryamāṇā rudanti ca |
mahāmegharavairghoraistrasyante ca muhurmuhuḥ ||
5.7.d:
महता पांसुवर्षेण पूर्यमाणा रुदन्ति च ।
महामेघरवैर्घोरैस्त्रस्यन्ते च मुहुर्मुहुः ॥
5.7.m: Filled [and covered] by a great shower of dust, they weep; / and they are terrified again and again by the terrible rumbles of great clouds.

5.7.s:
niśitāyudhavarṣeṇa bhidyamānāśca sarvataḥ |
mahākṣārāmbudhārābhiḥ sicyamānā vrajanti ca ||
5.7.d:
निशितायुधवर्षेण भिद्यमानाश्च सर्वतः ।
महाक्षाराम्बुधाराभिः सिच्यमाना व्रजन्ति च ॥
5.7.m: Pierced on all sides by a shower of sharp weapons, / and drenched with streams of water heavily laced with alkali, they march on.

5.7.s:
mahīśītena marutā rūkṣeṇa paruṣeṇa ca |
samantād bādhyamānāśca śuṣyante saṅkucanti ca ||
5.7.d:
महीशीतेन मरुता रूक्षेण परुषेण च ।
समन्ताद् बाध्यमानाश्च शुष्यन्ते सङ्कुचन्ति च ॥
5.7.m: Afflicted on all sides by a dry, harsh wind, cold as the ground, / they wither and shrink.

5.7.s:
itthaṃ mārgeṇa raudreṇa pātheyarahitena ca |
nirālambena durgeṇa nirjalena samantataḥ ||
5.7.d:
इत्थं मार्गेण रौद्रेण पाथेयरहितेन च ।
निरालम्बेन दुर्गेण निर्जलेन समन्ततः ॥
5.7.m: Thus, along a dreadful path, devoid of provisions, / without support, impassable, and entirely waterless,

5.7.s:
viṣameṇaiva mahatā nirjanāpāśrayeṇa ca |
tamorūpeṇa kaṣṭena sarvaduṣṭāśrayeṇa ca ||
5.7.d:
विषमेणैव महता निर्जनापाश्रयेण च ।
तमोरूपेण कष्टेन सर्वदुष्टाश्रयेण च ॥
5.7.m: exceedingly uneven, having no shelter of human beings, / enveloped in darkness, miserable, and the resort of all vicious [creatures],

5.7.s:
nīyante dehinaḥ sarve ye mūḍhāḥ pāpakarmiṇaḥ |
yamadūtairmahāghoraistadājñākāribhirbalāt ||
5.7.d:
नीयन्ते देहिनः सर्वे ये मूढाः पापकर्मिणः ।
यमदूतैर्महाघोरैस्तदाज्ञाकारिभिर्बलात् ॥
5.7.m: all embodied souls who are foolish evildoers / are dragged by force by the exceedingly terrible messengers of Yama, who carry out his commands.

5.7.s:
ekākinaḥ parādhīnā mitrabandhuvivarjitāḥ |
śocantaḥ svāni karmāṇi rudantaśca muhurmuhuḥ ||
5.7.d:
एकाकिनः पराधीना मित्रबन्धुविवर्जिताः ।
शोचन्तः स्वानि कर्माणि रुदन्तश्च मुहुर्मुहुः ॥
5.7.m: Alone, subservient to others, devoid of friends and kinsmen, / grieving over their own deeds and weeping again and again,

5.7.s:
pretā bhūtvā vivastrāśca śuṣkakaṇṭhauṣṭhatālukāḥ |
asaumyā bhayabhītāśca dahyamānāḥ kṣudhānvitāḥ ||
5.7.d:
प्रेता भूत्वा विवस्त्राश्च शुष्ककण्ठौष्ठतालुकाः ।
असौम्या भयभीताश्च दह्यमानाः क्षुधान्विताः ॥
5.7.m: having become ghosts, naked, their throats, lips, and palates parched, / unlovely, terrified with fear, burning, and afflicted with hunger,

5.7.s:
baddhāḥ śṛṅkhalayā keciduttā napādakā narāḥ |
kṛṣyante kṛṣyamāṇāśca yamadūtairbalotkaṭaiḥ ||
5.7.d:
बद्धाः शृङ्खलया केचिदुत्ता नपादका नराः ।
कृष्यन्ते कृष्यमाणाश्च यमदूतैर्बलोत्कटैः ॥
5.7.m: some men, bound with iron chains and lying with feet upturned, / are dragged along by the messengers of Yama of tremendous might.

5.7.s:
urasādhomukhāścānye ghṛṣyamāṇāḥ suduḥkhitāḥ |
keśapāśanibandhena saṅkṛṣyante ca rajjunā ||
5.7.d:
उरसाधोमुखाश्चान्ये घृष्यमाणाः सुदुःखिताः ।
केशपाशनिबन्धेन सङ्कृष्यन्ते च रज्जुना ॥
5.7.m: Others, lying face downward, scraped on their chests and suffering intensely, / are dragged along by a rope tied to their masses of hair.

5.7.s:
lalāṭe cāṅkuśenānye bhinnā duṣyanti dehinaḥ |
uttānāḥ kaṇṭakapathā kvacidaṅgāravartmanā ||
5.7.d:
ललाटे चाङ्कुशेनान्ये भिन्ना दुष्यन्ति देहिनः ।
उत्तानाः कण्टकपथा क्वचिदङ्गारवर्त्मना ॥
5.7.m: Other embodied beings, pierced on the forehead with a hook, suffer; / lying face upward, [dragged] over paths of thorns and sometimes along tracks of burning coals.

5.7.s:
paścād bāhunibaddhāśca jaṭhareṇa prapīḍitāḥ |
pūritāḥ śṛṅkhalābhiśca hastayośca sukīlitāḥ ||
5.7.d:
पश्चाद् बाहुनिबद्धाश्च जठरेण प्रपीडिताः ।
पूरिताः शृङ्खलाभिश्च हस्तयोश्च सुकीलिताः ॥
5.7.m: With their arms tied behind their backs, pressed upon their bellies, / heavily bound with chains, and securely nailed through the hands,

5.7.s:
grīvāpāśena kṛṣyante prayāntyanye suduḥkhitāḥ |
jihvāṅkuśapraveśena rajjvākṛṣyanta eva te ||
5.7.d:
ग्रीवापाशेन कृष्यन्ते प्रयान्त्यन्ये सुदुःखिताः ।
जिह्वाङ्कुशप्रवेशेन रज्ज्वाकृष्यन्त एव ते ॥
5.7.m: some, dragged by a noose around the neck, march on in utter misery; / others are dragged along by a rope inserted with a hook through the tongue.

5.7.s:
nāsābhedena rajjvā ca tvākṛṣyante tathāpare |
bhinnāḥ kapolayo rajjvā kṛṣyante'nye tathauṣṭhayoḥ ||
5.7.d:
नासाभेदेन रज्ज्वा च त्वाकृष्यन्ते तथापरे ।
भिन्नाः कपोलयो रज्ज्वा कृष्यन्तेऽन्ये तथौष्ठयोः ॥
5.7.m: Others still are dragged by a rope piercing the nose; / others, pierced through the cheeks or through the lips, are dragged by a rope.

5.7.s:
chinnāgrapādahastāśca chinnakarṇoṣṭhanāsikāḥ |
sañchinnaśiśnavṛṣaṇāḥ chinnabhinnāṅgasandhayaḥ ||
5.7.d:
छिन्नाग्रपादहस्ताश्च छिन्नकर्णोष्ठनासिकाः ।
सञ्छिन्नशिश्नवृषणाः छिन्नभिन्नाङ्गसन्धयः ॥
5.7.m: Their feet and hand tips severed, their ears, lips, and noses cut off, / their penises and testicles sliced away, their limbs and joints severed and shattered,

5.7.s:
ābhidyamānāḥ kuntaiśca bhidyamānāśca sāyakaiḥ |
itaścetaśca dhāvantaḥ krandamānā nirāśrayāḥ ||
5.7.d:
आभिद्यमानाः कुन्तैश्च भिद्यमानाश्च सायकैः ।
इतश्चेतश्च धावन्तः क्रन्दमाना निराश्रयाः ॥
5.7.m: pierced with spears and wounded with arrows, / running hither and thither, wailing, shelterless,

5.7.s:
mudgarairlohadaṇḍaiśca hanyamānā muhurmuhuḥ |
kaṇṭakairvividhairghorairjvalanārkasamaprabhaiḥ ||
5.7.d:
मुद्गरैर्लोहदण्डैश्च हन्यमाना मुहुर्मुहुः ।
कण्टकैर्विविधैर्घोरैर्ज्वलनार्कसमप्रभैः ॥
5.7.m: struck repeatedly with mallets and iron rods, / and with various terrible thorns blazing like the sun,

5.7.s:
bhindipālairvibhidyante sravataḥ pūyaśoṇitam |
śakṛtā kṛmidigdhāśca nīyante vivaśā narāḥ ||
5.7.d:
भिन्दिपालैर्विभिद्यन्ते स्रवतः पूयशोणितम् ।
शकृता कृमिदिग्धाश्च नीयन्ते विवशा नराः ॥
5.7.m: they are pierced with slings and javelins, exuding pus and blood; / smeared with feces and worms, the helpless men are led away.

5.7.s:
yācamānāśca salilamannaṃ vāpi bubhukṣitāḥ |
chāyāṃ prārthayamānāśca śītārtāścānalaṃ punaḥ ||
5.7.d:
याचमानाश्च सलिलमन्नं वापि बुभुक्षिताः ।
छायां प्रार्थयमानाश्च शीतार्ताश्चानलं पुनः ॥
5.7.m: Begging for water or food when hungry, / pleading for shade, or, when afflicted with cold, [pleading] again for fire,

5.7.s:
dānahīnāḥ prayāntyevaṃ prārthayantaḥ sukhaṃ narāḥ |
gṛhītadānapātheyāḥ sukhaṃ yānti yamālayam ||
5.7.d:
दानहीनाः प्रयान्त्येवं प्रार्थयन्तः सुखं नराः ।
गृहीतदानपाथेयाः सुखं यान्ति यमालयम् ॥
5.7.m: men destitute of gifts march thus, begging for comfort. / Those who carry the travel provisions of gifts go happily to Yama's abode.

5.7.s:
evaṃ nyāyena kaṣṭena prāptāḥ pretapuraṃ yadā |
prajñāpitāstato dūtairniveśyante yamāgrataḥ ||
5.7.d:
एवं न्यायेन कष्टेन प्राप्ताः प्रेतपुरं यदा ।
प्रज्ञापितास्ततो दूतैर्निवेश्यन्ते यमाग्रतः ॥
5.7.m: When, by this painful ordeal, they have reached the city of the dead, / announced by the messengers, they are ushered before Yama.

5.7.s:
tatra ye śubhakarmāṇastāṃstu sammānayedyamaḥ |
svāgatāsanadānena pādyārghyeṇa priyeṇa ca ||
5.7.d:
तत्र ये शुभकर्माणस्तांस्तु सम्मानयेद्यमः ।
स्वागतासनदानेन पाद्यार्घ्येण प्रियेण च ॥
5.7.m: There, Yama honors those who have performed good deeds / by welcoming them, offering a seat, water for the feet, respectful offerings, and pleasant words:

5.7.s:
dhanyā yūyaṃ mahātmāno nigamoditakāriṇaḥ |
yaiśca divyasukhārthāya bhavadbhiḥ sukṛtaṃ kṛtam ||
5.7.d:
धन्या यूयं महात्मानो निगमोदितकारिणः ।
यैश्च दिव्यसुखार्थाय भवद्भिः सुकृतं कृतम् ॥
5.7.m: “Blessed are you, noble souls, who act according to the Vedas, / by whom good deeds were performed for the sake of divine happiness!

5.7.s:
divyaṃ vimānamāruhya divyastrībhogabhūṣitam |
svargaṃ gacchadhvamamalaṃ sarvakāmasamanvitam ||
5.7.d:
दिव्यं विमानमारुह्य दिव्यस्त्रीभोगभूषितम् ।
स्वर्गं गच्छध्वममलं सर्वकामसमन्वितम् ॥
5.7.m: Ascend a celestial chariot adorned with the enjoyment of divine maidens, / and go to the immaculate heaven, endowed with all desires.

5.7.s:
tatra bhuktvā mahābhogānante puṇyasya saṅkṣayāt |
yatkiñcidalpamaśubhaṃ punastadiha bhokṣyatha ||
5.7.d:
तत्र भुक्त्वा महाभोगानन्ते पुण्यस्य सङ्क्षयात् ।
यत्किञ्चिदल्पमशुभं पुनस्तदिह भोक्ष्यथ ॥
5.7.m: Having enjoyed great pleasures there, at the end, upon the exhaustion of your merit, / whatever small amount of evil remains, you will experience it here.”

5.7.s:
dharmātmāno narā ye ca mitrabhūtā ivātmanaḥ |
saumyaṃ mukhaṃ prapaśyanti dharmarājanameva ca ||
5.7.d:
धर्मात्मानो नरा ये च मित्रभूता इवात्मनः ।
सौम्यं मुखं प्रपश्यन्ति धर्मराजनमेव च ॥
5.7.m: And those men of righteous soul, who are like friends to him, / behold the gentle face of the King of Dharma himself.

5.7.s:
ye punaḥ krūrakarmāṇaste paśyanti bhayānakam |
daṃṣṭrākarālavadanaṃ bhṛkuṭīkuṭilekṣaṇam ||
5.7.d:
ये पुनः क्रूरकर्माणस्ते पश्यन्ति भयानकम् ।
दंष्ट्राकरालवदनं भृकुटीकुटिलेक्षणम् ॥
5.7.m: Those, on the other hand, of cruel deeds behold a terrifying figure, / with a face dreadful with fangs, and eyes knit with frowns,

5.7.s:
ūrdhvakeśaṃ mahāśmaśrumūrdhvaprasphuritādharam |
aṣṭādaśabhujaṃ kruddhaṃ nīlāñjanacayopamam ||
5.7.d:
ऊर्ध्वकेशं महाश्मश्रुमूर्ध्वप्रस्फुरिताधरम् ।
अष्टादशभुजं क्रुद्धं नीलाञ्जनचयोपमम् ॥
5.7.m: with hair standing erect, a large beard, his upper lip trembling [in rage], / eighteen-armed, furious, resembling a heap of black collyrium,

5.7.s:
sarvāyudhoddhṛtakaraṃ sarvadaṇḍena tarjayan |
mahāmahiṣamārūḍhaṃ dīptāgnisamalocanam ||
5.7.d:
सर्वायुधोद्धृतकरं सर्वदण्डेन तर्जयन् ।
महामहिषमारूढं दीप्ताग्निसमलोचनम् ॥
5.7.m: his hands raised with all kinds of weapons, threatening with the staff of universal punishment, / mounted on a great buffalo, with eyes blazing like fire,

5.7.s:
raktamālyāmbaradharaṃ mahāmerumivocchritam |
pralayāmbudanirghoṣaṃ pibanniva mahodadhim ||
5.7.d:
रक्तमाल्याम्बरधरं महामेरुमिवोच्छ्रितम् ।
प्रलयाम्बुदनिर्घोषं पिबन्निव महोदधिम् ॥
5.7.m: wearing red garlands and garments, lofty as the great Meru, / with a voice like dissolution clouds, as if drinking the great ocean,

5.7.s:
grasantamiva śailendramudgirantamivānalam |
mṛtyuścaiva samīpasthaḥ kālānalasamaprabhaḥ ||
5.7.d:
ग्रसन्तमिव शैलेन्द्रमुद्गिरन्तमिवानलम् ।
मृत्युश्चैव समीपस्थः कालानलसमप्रभः ॥
5.7.m: as if swallowing the king of mountains, as if vomiting fire. / And standing near him was Mṛtyu, shining like the fire of cosmic dissolution,

5.7.s:
kālaścāñjanasaṅkāśaḥ kṛtāntaśca bhayānakaḥ |
mārī cogramahāmārī kālarātriśca dāruṇā ||
5.7.d:
कालश्चाञ्जनसङ्काशः कृतान्तश्च भयानकः ।
मारी चोग्रमहामारी कालरात्रिश्च दारुणा ॥
5.7.m: and Kāla resembling collyrium, and the terrifying Kṛtānta, / Mārī, the dreadful Mahāmārī, and terrible Kālarātri,

5.7.s:
vividhā vyādhayaḥ kuṣṭhā nānārūpā bhayāvahāḥ |
śaktiśūlāṅkuśadharāḥ pāśacakrāsipāṇayaḥ ||
5.7.d:
विविधा व्याधयः कुष्ठा नानारूपा भयावहाः ।
शक्तिशूलाङ्कुशधराः पाशचक्रासिपाणयः ॥
5.7.m: diverse diseases, leprosy, multiform and terrifying, / wielding javelins, spears, and goads, holding nooses, discuses, and swords in hand,

5.7.s:
vajratuṇḍadharā raudrāḥ kṣuratūṇadhanurddharāḥ |
nānāyudhadharāḥ sarve mahāvīrā bhayaṅkarāḥ ||
5.7.d:
वज्रतुण्डधरा रौद्राः क्षुरतूणधनुर्द्धराः ।
नानायुधधराः सर्वे महावीरा भयङ्कराः ॥
5.7.m: having diamond-hard beaks, fierce, bearing razors, quivers, and bows, / all bearing diverse weapons, mighty heroes, terrifying,

5.7.s:
asaṅkhyātā mahāvīrāḥ kālāñjanasamaprabhāḥ |
sarvāyudhodyatakarā yamadūtā bhayānakāḥ ||
5.7.d:
असङ्ख्याता महावीराः कालाञ्जनसमप्रभाः ।
सर्वायुधोद्यतकरा यमदूता भयानकाः ॥
5.7.m: innumerable mighty warriors, radiant like dark collyrium, / their hands raised with all kinds of weapons, terrifying messengers of Yama.

5.7.s:
anena paricāreṇa vṛtaṃ taṃ ghoradarśanam |
yamaṃ paśyanti pāpiṣṭhāścitraguptaṃ ca bhīṣaṇam ||
5.7.d:
अनेन परिचारेण वृतं तं घोरदर्शनम् ।
यमं पश्यन्ति पापिष्ठाश्चित्रगुप्तं च भीषणम् ॥
5.7.m: Surrounded by this retinue, of frightful appearance, / Yama is beheld by the sinners, as well as the terrifying Citragupta.

5.7.s:
nirbhartsayati cātyantaṃ yamastānpāpakarmaṇaḥ |
citraguptaśca bhagavān dharmavākyaiḥ prabodhayet ||
śrīgaṇeśāya namaḥ ||
śrīgaurīśaṅkarābhyāṃ namaḥ ||
śrīśivamahāpurāṇam ||
5.7.d:
निर्भर्त्सयति चात्यन्तं यमस्तान्पापकर्मणः ।
चित्रगुप्तश्च भगवान् धर्मवाक्यैः प्रबोधयेत् ॥
श्रीगणेशाय नमः ॥
श्रीगौरीशङ्कराभ्यां नमः ॥
श्रीशिवमहापुराणम् ॥
5.7.m:
Yama severely rebukes those evil-doers, / and the blessed Citragupta admonishes them with words of righteousness.

Homage to the auspicious Gaurī and Śaṅkara.

5.8.s:
citragupta uvāca |
bho bho duṣkṛtakarmāṇaḥ paradravyāpahārakāḥ |
garvitā rūpavīryeṇa paradārāvamardakāḥ ||
5.8.d:
चित्रगुप्त उवाच ।
भो भो दुष्कृतकर्माणः परद्रव्यापहारकाः ।
गर्विता रूपवीर्येण परदारावमर्दकाः ॥
5.8.m: Citragupta said: / “O, O evildoers, thieves of others' wealth, / proud of your beauty and prowess, violators of others' wives!

5.8.s:
yat svayaṃ kriyate karma tadidaṃ bhujyate punaḥ |
tatkimātmopaghātārthaṃ bhavadbhirduṣkṛtaṃ kṛtam ||
5.8.d:
यत् स्वयं क्रियते कर्म तदिदं भुज्यते पुनः ।
तत्किमात्मोपघातार्थं भवद्भिर्दुष्कृतं कृतम् ॥
5.8.m: Whatever deed is committed by oneself, that very deed is experienced again. / Why then was evil done by you for the destruction of your own selves?

5.8.s:
idānīṃ kiṃ pralapyadhvaṃ pīḍyamānāḥ svakarmabhiḥ |
bhujyantāṃ svāni karmāṇi nāsti doṣo hi kasyacit ||
5.8.d:
इदानीं किं प्रलप्यध्वं पीड्यमानाः स्वकर्मभिः ।
भुज्यन्तां स्वानि कर्माणि नास्ति दोषो हि कस्यचित् ॥
5.8.m: Why do you lament now, being tormented by your own deeds? / Let your own deeds be experienced; indeed, no one else is at fault.”

5.8.s:
sanatkumāra uvāca |
evaṃ te pṛthivīpālāḥ samprāptāstatsamīpataḥ |
svakīyaiḥ karmabhighaurairduṣkarmabaladarpiṇaḥ ||
5.8.d:
सनत्कुमार उवाच ।
एवं ते पृथिवीपालाः सम्प्राप्तास्तत्समीपतः ।
स्वकीयैः कर्मभिघौरैर्दुष्कर्मबलदर्पिणः ॥
5.8.m: Sanatkumāra said: / Thus those rulers of the earth arrived near him, / arrogant with the power of wicked acts, [dragged] by their own terrible deeds.

5.8.s:
tānapi krodhasaṃyuktaścitragupto mahāprabhuḥ |
saṃśikṣayati dharmajño yamarājānuśikṣayā ||
5.8.d:
तानपि क्रोधसंयुक्तश्चित्रगुप्तो महाप्रभुः ।
संशिक्षयति धर्मज्ञो यमराजानुशिक्षया ॥
5.8.m: The great lord Citragupta, who knows righteousness, filled with anger, / instructed them also according to the instructions of King Yama.

5.8.s:
citragupta uvāca |
bho bho nṛpā durācārāḥ prajāvidhvaṃsakāriṇaḥ |
alpakālasya rājyasya kṛte kiṃ duṣkṛtaṃ kṛtam ||
5.8.d:
चित्रगुप्त उवाच ।
भो भो नृपा दुराचाराः प्रजाविध्वंसकारिणः ।
अल्पकालस्य राज्यस्य कृते किं दुष्कृतं कृतम् ॥
5.8.m: Citragupta said: / “O, O kings of wicked conduct, destroyers of subjects! / For the sake of a kingdom of short duration, why was wickedness committed?

5.8.s:
rājyabhogena mohena balādanyāyataḥ prajāḥ |
yaddaṇḍitāḥ phalaṃ tasya bhujyatāmadhunā nṛpāḥ ||
5.8.d:
राज्यभोगेन मोहेन बलादन्यायतः प्रजाः ।
यद्दण्डिताः फलं तस्य भुज्यतामधुना नृपाः ॥
5.8.m: Because subjects were punished by force and unjustly out of delusion with the enjoyment of kingship, / O kings, let the fruit of that be tasted now!

5.8.s:
kva tadrājyaṃ kalatraṃ ca yadarthamaśubhaṃ kṛtam |
tatsarvaṃ samparityajya yūyamekākinaḥ sthitāḥ ||
5.8.d:
क्व तद्राज्यं कलत्रं च यदर्थमशुभं कृतम् ।
तत्सर्वं सम्परित्यज्य यूयमेकाकिनः स्थिताः ॥
5.8.m: Where is that kingdom and where is that wife for whose sake evil was done? / Having completely abandoned all that, you stand alone!

5.8.s:
paśyāmi tadbalaṃ naṣṭaṃ yena vidhvaṃsitāḥ prajāḥ |
yamadūtairyojyamānā adhunā kīdṛśaṃ bhavet ||
5.8.d:
पश्यामि तद्बलं नष्टं येन विध्वंसिताः प्रजाः ।
यमदूतैर्योज्यमाना अधुना कीदृशं भवेत् ॥
5.8.m: I see that power destroyed by which the subjects were crushed. / Now, being bound by Yama's messengers, what will it be like?”

5.8.s:
sanatkumāra uvāca |
evaṃ bahuvidhairvākyairupalabdhā yamena te |
svāni karmāṇi śocanti tūṣṇīṃ tiṣṭhanti pārthivāḥ ||
5.8.d:
सनत्कुमार उवाच ।
एवं बहुविधैर्वाक्यैरुपलब्धा यमेन ते ।
स्वानि कर्माणि शोचन्ति तूष्णीं तिष्ठन्ति पार्थिवाः ॥
5.8.m: Sanatkumāra said: / Having been thus reprimanded by Yama with many kinds of words, / those kings lamented their own deeds and stood silent.

5.8.s:
iti karma samuddiśya nṛpāṇāṃ dharmarāḍ yamaḥ |
tatpāpapaṅkaśuddhyarthamidaṃ dūtān bravīti ca ||
5.8.d:
इति कर्म समुद्दिश्य नृपाणां धर्मराड् यमः ।
तत्पापपङ्कशुद्ध्यर्थमिदं दूतान् ब्रवीति च ॥
5.8.m: Having thus pointed out the actions of the kings, Yama, the King of Dharma, / spoke this to the messengers for the cleansing of the mire of their sins:

5.8.s:
yamarāja uvāca |
bho bhoścaṇḍa mahācaṇḍa gṛhītvā nṛpatīnbalāt |
niyamena viśudyadhvaṃ krameṇa narakāgniṣu ||
5.8.d:
यमराज उवाच ।
भो भोश्चण्ड महाचण्ड गृहीत्वा नृपतीन्बलात् ।
नियमेन विशुद्यध्वं क्रमेण नरकाग्निषु ॥
5.8.m: Yama said: / "Ho there, Caṇḍa, Mahācaṇḍa! Seize the kings by force! / Cleanse [them] systematically in order in the fires of hell."

5.8.s:
sanatkumāra uvāca |
tataḥ śīghraṃ samādāya nṛpān saṅgṛhya pādayoḥ |
bhrāmayitvā tu vegena nikṣipyordhvaṃ pragṛhya ca ||
5.8.d:
सनत्कुमार उवाच ।
ततः शीघ्रं समादाय नृपान् सङ्गृह्य पादयोः ।
भ्रामयित्वा तु वेगेन निक्षिप्योर्ध्वं प्रगृह्य च ॥
5.8.m: Sanatkumāra said: / Then, swiftly seizing the kings and grabbing them by the feet, / whirling [them] around with velocity, hurling them upward, and catching them,

5.8.s:
sarvaprāyeṇa mahatātīva tapte śilātale |
āsphālayanti tarasā vajreṇeva mahādrumān ||
5.8.d:
सर्वप्रायेण महतातीव तप्ते शिलातले ।
आस्फालयन्ति तरसा वज्रेणेव महाद्रुमान् ॥
5.8.m: they dash them violently against a huge, excessively heated stone slab, / as if striking great trees with a thunderbolt.

5.8.s:
tataḥ sa raktaṃ śrotreṇa sravate jarjarīkṛtaḥ |
niḥsaṃjñaḥ sa tadā dehī niśceṣṭaḥ samprajāyate ||
5.8.d:
ततः स रक्तं श्रोत्रेण स्रवते जर्जरीकृतः ।
निःसंज्ञः स तदा देही निश्चेष्टः सम्प्रजायते ॥
5.8.m: Then, battered to pieces, blood flows from their ears; / the embodied soul then becomes unconscious and motionless.

5.8.s:
tataḥ sa vāyunā spṛṣṭaḥ sa tairujjīvitaḥ punaḥ |
tataḥ pāpaviśuddhyarthaṃ kṣipanti narakārṇave ||
5.8.d:
ततः स वायुना स्पृष्टः स तैरुज्जीवितः पुनः ।
ततः पापविशुद्ध्यर्थं क्षिपन्ति नरकार्णवे ॥
5.8.m: Then, touched by the wind, revived again by them, / they cast them into the ocean of hell for the cleansing of their sins.

5.8.s:
aṣṭāviṃśatisaṅkhyābhiḥ kṣityadhaḥ saptakoṭayaḥ |
saptamasya talasyānte ghore tamasi saṃsthitaḥ ||
5.8.d:
अष्टाविंशतिसङ्ख्याभिः क्षित्यधः सप्तकोटयः ।
सप्तमस्य तलस्यान्ते घोरे तमसि संस्थितः ॥
5.8.m: Below the earth are seven regions of ten million, numbering twenty-eight [categories]; / situated at the end of the seventh level, in dreadful darkness,

5.8.s:
ghorākhyā prathamā koṭiḥ sughorā tadadhaḥ sthitā |
atighorā mahāghorā ghorarūpā ca pañcamī ||
5.8.d:
घोराख्या प्रथमा कोटिः सुघोरा तदधः स्थिता ।
अतिघोरा महाघोरा घोररूपा च पञ्चमी ॥
5.8.m: the first [level of] ten million is named Ghorā, below it is Sughorā, / Atighorā, Mahāghorā, and the fifth is Ghorarūpā;

5.8.s:
ṣaṣṭhī talātalākhyā ca saptamī ca bhayānakā |
aṣṭamī kālarātriśca navamī ca bhayotkaṭā ||
5.8.d:
षष्ठी तलातलाख्या च सप्तमी च भयानका ।
अष्टमी कालरात्रिश्च नवमी च भयोत्कटा ॥
5.8.m: the sixth is called Talātalā, and the seventh is Bhayānakā; / the eighth is Kālarātri, and the ninth is Bhayotkaṭā;

5.8.s:
daśamī tadadhaścaṇḍā mahācaṇḍā tato'pyadhaḥ |
caṇḍakolāhalā cānyā pracaṇḍā caṇḍanāyikā ||
5.8.d:
दशमी तदधश्चण्डा महाचण्डा ततोऽप्यधः ।
चण्डकोलाहला चान्या प्रचण्डा चण्डनायिका ॥
5.8.m: beneath it, the tenth is Caṇḍā, and below that is Mahācaṇḍā; / another is Caṇḍakolāhalā, Pracaṇḍā, and Caṇḍanāyikā;

5.8.s:
padmā padmāvatī bhītā bhīmā bhīṣaṇanāyikā |
karālā vikarālā ca vajrā viṃśatimā smṛtā ||
5.8.d:
पद्मा पद्मावती भीता भीमा भीषणनायिका ।
कराला विकराला च वज्रा विंशतिमा स्मृता ॥
5.8.m: Padmā, Padmāvatī, Bhītā, Bhīmā, Bhīṣaṇanāyikā, / Karālā, Vikarālā, and the twentieth is remembered as Vajrā;

5.8.s:
trikoṇā pañcakoṇā ca sudīrghā cākhilārtidā |
samā bhīmabalābhogrā dīptaprāyeti cāṣṭamī ||
5.8.d:
त्रिकोणा पञ्चकोणा च सुदीर्घा चाखिलार्तिदा ।
समा भीमबलाभोग्रा दीप्तप्रायेति चाष्टमी ॥
5.8.m: Trikoṇā, Pañcakoṇā, Sudīrghā, Akhilārtidā, / Samā, Bhīmabalā, Bhogrā, and the twenty-eighth is Dīptaprāyā.

5.8.s:
iti te nāmataḥ proktā ghorā narakakoṭayaḥ |
aṣṭāviṃśatirevaitāḥ pāpānāṃ yātanātmikāḥ ||
5.8.d:
इति ते नामतः प्रोक्ता घोरा नरककोटयः ।
अष्टाविंशतिरेवैताः पापानां यातनात्मिकाः ॥
5.8.m: Thus the dreadful hell-regions of ten million have been declared to you by name; / these twenty-eight indeed consist of torments for sinners.

5.8.s:
tāsāṃ krameṇa vijñeyāḥ pañca pañcaiva nāyakāḥ |
pratyekaṃ sarvakoṭīnāṃ nāmataḥ sannibodhata ||
5.8.d:
तासां क्रमेण विज्ञेयाः पञ्च पञ्चैव नायकाः ।
प्रत्येकं सर्वकोटीनां नामतः सन्निबोधत ॥
5.8.m: Five leaders each are to be known successively for them; / listen to each of them by name for all the regions of ten million:

5.8.s:
rauravaḥ prathamasteṣāṃ rudante yatra dehinaḥ |
mahārauravapīḍābhirmahānto'pi rudanti ca ||
5.8.d:
रौरवः प्रथमस्तेषां रुदन्ते यत्र देहिनः ।
महारौरवपीडाभिर्महान्तोऽपि रुदन्ति च ॥
5.8.m: Raurava is the first of them, where embodied beings weep, / and even great souls weep from the torments of Mahāraurava;

5.8.s:
tataḥ śītaṃ tathā coṣṇaṃ pañcādyā nāyakāḥ smṛtāḥ |
sughoraḥ sumahātīkṣṇastathā sañjīvanaḥ smṛtaḥ ||
5.8.d:
ततः शीतं तथा चोष्णं पञ्चाद्या नायकाः स्मृताः ।
सुघोरः सुमहातीक्ष्णस्तथा सञ्जीवनः स्मृतः ॥
5.8.m: then Śīta and Uṣṇa—these are remembered as the first five leaders; / Sughora, Sumahātīkṣṇa, and Sañjīvana is remembered;

5.8.s:
mahātamo vilomaśca vilopaścāpi kaṇṭakaḥ |
tīvravegaḥ karālaśca vikarālaḥ prakampanaḥ ||
5.8.d:
महातमो विलोमश्च विलोपश्चापि कण्टकः ।
तीव्रवेगः करालश्च विकरालः प्रकम्पनः ॥
5.8.m: Mahātamas, Viloma, Vilopa, and Kaṇṭaka; / Tīvravega, Karāla, Vikarāla, Prakampana;

5.8.s:
mahāvakraśca kālaśca kālasūtraḥ pragarjanaḥ |
sūcīmukhaḥ sunetiśca khādakaḥ suprapīḍanaḥ ||
5.8.d:
महावक्रश्च कालश्च कालसूत्रः प्रगर्जनः ।
सूचीमुखः सुनेतिश्च खादकः सुप्रपीडनः ॥
5.8.m: Mahāvakra, Kāla, Kālasūtra, Pragarjana; / Sūcīmukha, Suneti, Khādaka, Suprapīḍana;

5.8.s:
kumbhīpākasupākau ca krakacaścātidāruṇaḥ |
aṅgārarāśibhavanaṃ medo'sṛkprahitastataḥ ||
5.8.d:
कुम्भीपाकसुपाकौ च क्रकचश्चातिदारुणः ।
अङ्गारराशिभवनं मेदोऽसृक्प्रहितस्ततः ॥
5.8.m: Kumbhīpāka and Supāka, Krakaca, and Atidāruṇa; / Aṅgārarāśibhavana, and then Medo'sṛkprahita;

5.8.s:
tīkṣṇatuṇḍaśca śakunirmahāsaṃvartakaḥ kratuḥ |
taptajantuḥ paṅkalepaḥ pratimāṃsastrapūdbhavaḥ ||
5.8.d:
तीक्ष्णतुण्डश्च शकुनिर्महासंवर्तकः क्रतुः ।
तप्तजन्तुः पङ्कलेपः प्रतिमांसस्त्रपूद्भवः ॥
5.8.m: Tīkṣṇatuṇḍa, Śakuni, Mahāsaṃvartaka, Kratu; / Taptajantu, Paṅkalepa, Pratimāṃsa, Trapūdbhava;

5.8.s:
ucchvāsaḥ sunirucchvāso sudīrghaḥ kūṭaśālmaliḥ |
duriṣṭaḥ sumahāvādaḥ pravāhaḥ supratāpanaḥ ||
5.8.d:
उच्छ्वासः सुनिरुच्छ्वासो सुदीर्घः कूटशाल्मलिः ।
दुरिष्टः सुमहावादः प्रवाहः सुप्रतापनः ॥
5.8.m: Ucchvāsa, Sunirucchvāsa, Sudīrgha, Kūṭaśālmali; / Duriṣṭa, Sumahāvāda, Pravāha, Supratāpana;

5.8.s:
tato megho vṛṣaḥ śālmaḥ siṃhavyāghragajānanāḥ |
śvasūkarājamahiṣaghūkakokavṛkānanāḥ ||
5.8.d:
ततो मेघो वृषः शाल्मः सिंहव्याघ्रगजाननाः ।
श्वसूकराजमहिषघूककोकवृकाननाः ॥
5.8.m: then Megha, Vṛṣa, Śālma, those with faces of lions, tigers, and elephants; / those with faces of dogs, boars, goats, buffaloes, owls, cuckoos, and wolves;

5.8.s:
grāhakumbhīnanakrākhyāḥ sarpakūrmākhyavāyasāḥ |
gṛdhrolūkahalaukākhyāḥ śārdūlakrathakarkaṭāḥ ||
5.8.d:
ग्राहकुम्भीननक्राख्याः सर्पकूर्माख्यवायसाः ।
गृध्रोलूकहलौकाख्याः शार्दूलक्रथकर्कटाः ॥
5.8.m: those named Grāha, Kumbhīna, and Nakra, the serpents, the tortoises, and the crows; / those named vultures, owls, and leeches, tigers, Krathas, and crabs;

5.8.s:
maṇḍūkaḥ pūtivaktrāśca raktākṣaḥ pūtimṛttikāḥ |
kaṇadhūmrastathāgniśca kṛmigandhivapustathā ||
5.8.d:
मण्डूकः पूतिवक्त्राश्च रक्ताक्षः पूतिमृत्तिकाः ।
कणधूम्रस्तथाग्निश्च कृमिगन्धिवपुस्तथा ॥
5.8.m: Maṇḍūka, Pūtivaktra, Raktākṣa, Pūtimṛttikā, / Kaṇadhūmra, Agni, and Kṛmigandhivapu;

5.8.s:
agnīdhraścāpratiṣṭhaśca rudhirābhaḥ śvabhojanaḥ |
lālābhakṣāntrabhakṣau ca sarvabhakṣaḥ sudāruṇaḥ ||
5.8.d:
अग्नीध्रश्चाप्रतिष्ठश्च रुधिराभः श्वभोजनः ।
लालाभक्षान्त्रभक्षौ च सर्वभक्षः सुदारुणः ॥
5.8.m: Agnīdhra, Apratiṣṭha, Rudhirābha, Śvabhojana, / Lālābhakṣa, Antrabhakṣa, Sarvabhakṣa, Sudāruṇa;

5.8.s:
kaṇṭakaḥ suviśālaśca vikaṭaḥ kaṭapūtanaḥ |
ambarīṣaḥ kaṭāhaśca kaṣṭā vaitaraṇī nadī ||
5.8.d:
कण्टकः सुविशालश्च विकटः कटपूतनः ।
अम्बरीषः कटाहश्च कष्टा वैतरणी नदी ॥
5.8.m: Kaṇṭaka, Suviśāla, Vikaṭa, Kaṭapūtana, / Ambarīṣa, Kaṭāha, and the painful Vaitaraṇī river;

5.8.s:
sutaptalohaśayana ekapādaḥ prapūraṇaḥ |
asitālavanaṃ ghoramasthibhaṅgaḥ supūraṇaḥ ||
5.8.d:
सुतप्तलोहशयन एकपादः प्रपूरणः ।
असितालवनं घोरमस्थिभङ्गः सुपूरणः ॥
5.8.m: Sutaptalohaśayana, Ekapāda, Prapūraṇa, / the terrible Asitālavana, Asthibhaṅga, Supūraṇa;

5.8.s:
vilātaso'suyantropi kūṭapāśaḥ pramardanaḥ |
mahācūrarṇo'sucūrṇo'pi taptalohamayaṃ tathā ||
5.8.d:
विलातसोऽसुयन्त्रोपि कूटपाशः प्रमर्दनः ।
महाचूरर्णोऽसुचूर्णोऽपि तप्तलोहमयं तथा ॥
5.8.m: Vilātasa, Asuyantra, Kūṭapāśa, Pramardana, / Mahācūrṇa, Asucūrṇa, and Taptalohamaya;

5.8.s:
parvataḥ kṣuradhārā ca tathā yamalaparvataḥ |
mūtraviṣṭhāśrukūpaśca kṣārakūpaśca śītalaḥ ||
5.8.d:
पर्वतः क्षुरधारा च तथा यमलपर्वतः ।
मूत्रविष्ठाश्रुकूपश्च क्षारकूपश्च शीतलः ॥
5.8.m: Parvata, Kṣuradhārā, and the Yamalaparvata; / Mūtraviṣṭhāśrukūpa, Kṣārakūpa, and Śītala;

5.8.s:
musalolūkhalaṃ yantraṃ śilāśakaṭalāṅgalam |
tālapatrāsigahanaṃ mahāśakaṭamaṇḍapam ||
5.8.d:
मुसलोलूखलं यन्त्रं शिलाशकटलाङ्गलम् ।
तालपत्रासिगहनं महाशकटमण्डपम् ॥
5.8.m: Musalolūkhala, Yantra, Śilāśakaṭalāṅgala, / Tālapatrāsigahana, Mahāśakaṭamaṇḍapa;

5.8.s:
sammohamasthibhaṅgaśca taptaścalamayoguḍam |
bahuduḥkhaṃ mahākleśaḥ kaśmalaṃ samalaṃ malāt ||
5.8.d:
सम्मोहमस्थिभङ्गश्च तप्तश्चलमयोगुडम् ।
बहुदुःखं महाक्लेशः कश्मलं समलं मलात् ॥
5.8.m: Sammoha, Asthibhaṅga, Taptaścalamayoguḍa, / Bahuduḥkha, Mahākleśa, Kaśmala, Samala, Malāt;

5.8.s:
hālāhalo virūpaśca svarūpaśca yamānugaḥ |
ekapādastripādaśca tīvraścācīvaraṃ tamaḥ ||
5.8.d:
हालाहलो विरूपश्च स्वरूपश्च यमानुगः ।
एकपादस्त्रिपादश्च तीव्रश्चाचीवरं तमः ॥
5.8.m: Hālāhala, Virūpa, Svarūpa, Yamānuga, / Ekapāda, Tripāda, Tīvra, and Acīvaratamas;

5.8.s:
aṣṭāviṃśatirityete kramaśaḥ pañcapañcakam |
koṭīnāmānupūrvyeṇa pañca pañcaiva nāyakāḥ ||
5.8.d:
अष्टाविंशतिरित्येते क्रमशः पञ्चपञ्चकम् ।
कोटीनामानुपूर्व्येण पञ्च पञ्चैव नायकाः ॥
5.8.m: these twenty-eight [groups] are thus in order groups of five; / following the sequence of the tens of millions, there are five leaders for each.

5.8.s:
rauravāya prabodhyante narakāṇāṃ śataṃ smṛtam |
catvāriṃśacca tatproktaṃ mahānarakamaṇḍalam ||
5.8.d:
रौरवाय प्रबोध्यन्ते नरकाणां शतं स्मृतम् ।
चत्वारिंशच्च तत्प्रोक्तं महानरकमण्डलम् ॥
5.8.m: Beginning with Raurava, one hundred and forty hells / are known as that great realm of hell.

5.8.s:
iti te vyāsa samproktā narakasya sthitirmayā |
prasaṅkhyānācca vairāgyaṃ śṛṇu pāpagatiṃ ca tām ||
śrīgaṇeśāya namaḥ ||
śrīgaurīśaṅkarābhyāṃ namaḥ ||
śrīśivamahāpurāṇam ||
5.8.d:
इति ते व्यास सम्प्रोक्ता नरकस्य स्थितिर्मया ।
प्रसङ्ख्यानाच्च वैराग्यं शृणु पापगतिं च ताम् ॥
श्रीगणेशाय नमः ॥
श्रीगौरीशङ्कराभ्यां नमः ॥
श्रीशिवमहापुराणम् ॥
5.8.m: Thus, O Vyāsa, has the layout of hell been described to you by me; / and hear of the state of sinners that leads to detachment through reflection.

5.9.s:
sanatkumāra uvāca |
eṣu pāpāḥ prapacyante śoṣyante narakāgniṣu |
yātanābhirvicitrābhirāsvakarmakṣayād bhṛśam ||
5.9.d:
सनत्कुमार उवाच ।
एषु पापाः प्रपच्यन्ते शोष्यन्ते नरकाग्निषु ।
यातनाभिर्विचित्राभिरास्वकर्मक्षयाद् भृशम् ॥
5.9.m: Sanatkumāra said: / In these, the wicked are cooked and dried in hellfires / with diverse torments violently until the exhaustion of their own deeds.

5.9.s:
svamalaprakṣayādyadvadagnau dhāsyanti dhātavaḥ |
tatra pāpakṣayātpāpā narāḥ karmānurūpataḥ ||
5.9.d:
स्वमलप्रक्षयाद्यद्वदग्नौ धास्यन्ति धातवः ।
तत्र पापक्षयात्पापा नराः कर्मानुरूपतः ॥
5.9.m: Just as ores melt in fire through the destruction of their dross, / so there do sinful men [suffer] according to their deeds until the destruction of sins.

5.9.s:
sugāḍhaṃ hastayorbaddhvā tataḥ śṛṅkhalayā narāḥ |
mahāvṛkṣāgraśākhāsu lambyante yamakiṅkaraiḥ ||
5.9.d:
सुगाढं हस्तयोर्बद्ध्वा ततः शृङ्खलया नराः ।
महावृक्षाग्रशाखासु लम्ब्यन्ते यमकिङ्करैः ॥
5.9.m: Then, having bound the men tightly by the hands with a chain, / they are suspended from the top branches of great trees by the servants of Yama.

5.9.s:
tataste sarvayatnena kṣiptā dolanti kiṅkaraiḥ |
domyantaścātivegena visaṃjñā yānti yojanam ||
5.9.d:
ततस्ते सर्वयत्नेन क्षिप्ता दोलन्ति किङ्करैः ।
दोम्यन्तश्चातिवेगेन विसंज्ञा यान्ति योजनम् ॥
5.9.m: Then, pushed with all their might, they swing from the servants; / and being tossed with extreme speed, they lose consciousness and traverse a yojana.

5.9.s:
antarikṣasthitānāṃ ca lohabhāraśataṃ punaḥ |
pādayorbadhyate teṣāṃ yamadūtairmahābalaiḥ ||
5.9.d:
अन्तरिक्षस्थितानां च लोहभारशतं पुनः ।
पादयोर्बध्यते तेषां यमदूतैर्महाबलैः ॥
5.9.m: And while they are suspended in the air, a weight of a hundred iron [bars] / is again tied to their feet by the mighty messengers of Yama.

5.9.s:
tena bhāreṇa mahatā prabhṛśaṃ tāḍitā narāḥ |
dhyāyanti svāni karmāṇi tūṣṇīṃ tiṣṭhanti niścalāḥ ||
5.9.d:
तेन भारेण महता प्रभृशं ताडिता नराः ।
ध्यायन्ति स्वानि कर्माणि तूष्णीं तिष्ठन्ति निश्चलाः ॥
5.9.m: Struck violently by that great weight, / the men meditate upon their own actions and remain motionless in silence.

5.9.s:
tato'ṅkuśairagnivarṇairlohadaṇḍaiśca dāruṇaiḥ |
hanyante kiṅkaraighoraiḥ samantātpāpakarmiṇaḥ ||
5.9.d:
ततोऽङ्कुशैरग्निवर्णैर्लोहदण्डैश्च दारुणैः ।
हन्यन्ते किङ्करैघोरैः समन्तात्पापकर्मिणः ॥
5.9.m: Then the evildoers are beaten on all sides by the dreadful servants / with fire-colored iron hooks and cruel iron clubs.

5.9.s:
tataḥ kṣāreṇa dīptena vahnerapi viśeṣataḥ |
samantataḥ pralipyante tīvreṇa tu punaḥ punaḥ ||
5.9.d:
ततः क्षारेण दीप्तेन वह्नेरपि विशेषतः ।
समन्ततः प्रलिप्यन्ते तीव्रेण तु पुनः पुनः ॥
5.9.m: Then with caustic fluid brighter than even fire, / they are smeared on all sides again and again with intense [pain].

5.9.s:
drutenātyantaliptena kṛttāṅgā jarjarīkṛtāḥ |
punarvidārya cāṅgāni śirasaḥ prabhṛti kramāt ||
5.9.d:
द्रुतेनात्यन्तलिप्तेन कृत्ताङ्गा जर्जरीकृताः ।
पुनर्विदार्य चाङ्गानि शिरसः प्रभृति क्रमात् ॥
5.9.m: Their limbs torn and shattered, entirely smeared with molten [liquids], / their limbs being split again, in order beginning from the head,

5.9.s:
vṛntākavatprapacyante taptalohakaṭāhakaiḥ |
viṣṭhāpūrṇe tathā kūpe kṛmīṇāṃ nicaye punaḥ ||
5.9.d:
वृन्ताकवत्प्रपच्यन्ते तप्तलोहकटाहकैः ।
विष्ठापूर्णे तथा कूपे कृमीणां निचये पुनः ॥
5.9.m: they are cooked like eggplants in heated iron cauldrons, / and again in a well full of feces and a multitude of worms.

5.9.s:
medo'sṛkpūyapūrṇāyāṃ vāpyāṃ kṣipyanti te punaḥ |
bhakṣyante kṛmibhistīkṣṇairlohatuṇḍaiśca vāyasaiḥ ||
5.9.d:
मेदोऽसृक्पूयपूर्णायां वाप्यां क्षिप्यन्ति ते पुनः ।
भक्ष्यन्ते कृमिभिस्तीक्ष्णैर्लोहतुण्डैश्च वायसैः ॥
5.9.m: Again, they are thrown into a pool full of fat, blood, and pus; / they are devoured by sharp worms and iron-beaked crows,

5.9.s:
śvabhirdeṃśairvṛkairvyāghrai raudraiśca vikṛtānanaiḥ |
pacyante matsyavaccāpi pradīptāṅgārarāśiṣu ||
5.9.d:
श्वभिर्देंशैर्वृकैर्व्याघ्रै रौद्रैश्च विकृताननैः ।
पच्यन्ते मत्स्यवच्चापि प्रदीप्ताङ्गारराशिषु ॥
5.9.m: by dogs, biting flies, wolves, tigers, and fierce [beasts] with deformed faces; / and they are cooked like fish on heaps of blazing coals.

5.9.s:
bhinnāḥ śūlaiḥ sutīkṣṇaiśca narāḥ pāpena karmaṇā |
tailayantreṣu cākramya ghoraiḥ karmabhirātmanaḥ ||
5.9.d:
भिन्नाः शूलैः सुतीक्ष्णैश्च नराः पापेन कर्मणा ।
तैलयन्त्रेषु चाक्रम्य घोरैः कर्मभिरात्मनः ॥
5.9.m: Pierced with very sharp pikes, men through sinful action, / forced into oil-presses on account of their own dreadful deeds,

5.9.s:
tilā iva prapīḍyante cakrākhye janapiṇḍakāḥ |
bhrajyante cātape taptalohabhāṇḍeṣvanekadhā ||
5.9.d:
तिला इव प्रपीड्यन्ते चक्राख्ये जनपिण्डकाः ।
भ्रज्यन्ते चातपे तप्तलोहभाण्डेष्वनेकधा ॥
5.9.m: the masses of people are crushed like sesame seeds in the [press] called Cakra; / and they are roasted in many ways in iron pots heated in the blazing heat,

5.9.s:
tailapūrṇakaṭāheṣu sutapteṣu punaḥpunaḥ |
bahudhā pacyate jihvā prapīḍyorasi pādayoḥ ||
5.9.d:
तैलपूर्णकटाहेषु सुतप्तेषु पुनःपुनः ।
बहुधा पच्यते जिह्वा प्रपीड्योरसि पादयोः ॥
5.9.m: in caldrons filled with oil and intensely heated again and again. / The tongue is cooked in various ways, after crushing the chest and the two feet.

5.9.s:
yātanāśca mahatyo'tra śarīrasyāti sarvataḥ |
niḥśeṣanarakeṣvevaṃ kramanti kramaśo narāḥ ||
5.9.d:
यातनाश्च महत्योऽत्र शरीरस्याति सर्वतः ।
निःशेषनरकेष्वेवं क्रमन्ति क्रमशो नराः ॥
5.9.m: Here there are severe torments of the body on every side; / thus men pass step by step through all the hells without exception.

5.9.s:
narakeṣu ca sarveṣu vicitrā yamayātanāḥ |
yāmyaiśca dīyate vyāsa sarvāṅgeṣu sukaṣṭadāḥ ||
5.9.d:
नरकेषु च सर्वेषु विचित्रा यमयातनाः ।
याम्यैश्च दीयते व्यास सर्वाङ्गेषु सुकष्टदाः ॥
5.9.m: And in all the hells, diverse torments of Yama / are inflicted on all limbs by Yama's servants, causing terrible suffering, O Vyāsa.

5.9.s:
jvaladaṅgāramādāya mukhamāpūrya tāḍyate |
tataḥ kṣāreṇa dīptena tāmreṇa ca punaḥpunaḥ ||
5.9.d:
ज्वलदङ्गारमादाय मुखमापूर्य ताड्यते ।
ततः क्षारेण दीप्तेन ताम्रेण च पुनःपुनः ॥
5.9.m: Taking a burning coal and stuffing the mouth, [the sinner] is beaten; / then with burning caustic and molten copper again and again,

5.9.s:
ghṛtenātyantataptena tadā tailena tanmukham |
itastataḥ pīḍayitvā bhṛśamāpūrya hanyate ||
5.9.d:
घृतेनात्यन्ततप्तेन तदा तैलेन तन्मुखम् ।
इतस्ततः पीडयित्वा भृशमापूर्य हन्यते ॥
5.9.m: and then with intensely heated ghee and oil, pressing that mouth / this way and that, stuffing it completely, he is struck.

5.9.s:
viṣṭhābhiḥ kṛmibhiścāpi pūryamāṇāḥ kvacit kvacit |
pariṣvajanti cātyugrāṃ pradīptāṃ lohaśālmalīm ||
5.9.d:
विष्ठाभिः कृमिभिश्चापि पूर्यमाणाः क्वचित् क्वचित् ।
परिष्वजन्ति चात्युग्रां प्रदीप्तां लोहशाल्मलीम् ॥
5.9.m: Being stuffed in some places with feces and worms, / they embrace the intensely fierce, blazing iron silk-cotton tree.

5.9.s:
hanyante pṛṣṭhadeśe ca punardīptairmahāghanaiḥ |
dantureṇādikuṇṭhena krakacena balīsayā ||
5.9.d:
हन्यन्ते पृष्ठदेशे च पुनर्दीप्तैर्महाघनैः ।
दन्तुरेणादिकुण्ठेन क्रकचेन बलीसया ॥
5.9.m: They are beaten on the back again with blazing heavy hammers, / with a jagged, exceedingly blunt saw, and with a heavy mallet.

5.9.s:
śiraḥprabhṛti pīḍyante ghoraiḥ karmabhirātmajaiḥ |
khādyante ca svamāṃsāni pīyate śoṇitaṃ svakam ||
5.9.d:
शिरःप्रभृति पीड्यन्ते घोरैः कर्मभिरात्मजैः ।
खाद्यन्ते च स्वमांसानि पीयते शोणितं स्वकम् ॥
5.9.m: Beginning from the head, they are tormented by the terrible actions born of themselves; / their own flesh is eaten and their own blood is drunk.

5.9.s:
annaṃ pānaṃ na dattaṃ yaiḥ sarvadā svātmapoṣakaiḥ |
ikṣuvatte prapīḍyante jarjarīkṛtya mudgaraiḥ ||
5.9.d:
अन्नं पानं न दत्तं यैः सर्वदा स्वात्मपोषकैः ।
इक्षुवत्ते प्रपीड्यन्ते जर्जरीकृत्य मुद्गरैः ॥
5.9.m: Those by whom food and drink were never given, nourishing only themselves, / are crushed like sugarcane, having been shattered with mallets.

5.9.s:
asitālavane ghore chidyante khaṇḍaśastataḥ |
sūcībhirbhinnasarvāṅgāḥ taptaśūlāgraropitāḥ ||
5.9.d:
असितालवने घोरे छिद्यन्ते खण्डशस्ततः ।
सूचीभिर्भिन्नसर्वाङ्गाः तप्तशूलाग्ररोपिताः ॥
5.9.m: Then, in the terrible forest of sword-leaves, they are cut into pieces; / all their limbs pierced with needles, they are impaled upon the tips of heated pikes.

5.9.s:
sañcālyamānā bahuśaḥ kliśyante na mriyanti ca |
tathā ca taccharīrāṇi sukhaduḥkhasahāni ca ||
5.9.d:
सञ्चाल्यमाना बहुशः क्लिश्यन्ते न म्रियन्ति च ।
तथा च तच्छरीराणि सुखदुःखसहानि च ॥
5.9.m: Shaken repeatedly, they suffer and do not die; / for their bodies are capable of enduring pleasure and pain.

5.9.s:
dehādutpāṭya māṃsāni bhidyante svaiśca mudgaraiḥ |
danturākṛtibhirghorairyamadūtairbalotkaṭaiḥ ||
5.9.d:
देहादुत्पाट्य मांसानि भिद्यन्ते स्वैश्च मुद्गरैः ।
दन्तुराकृतिभिर्घोरैर्यमदूतैर्बलोत्कटैः ॥
5.9.m: Flesh is torn from the body and shattered with their own clubs / by fierce servants of Yama of jagged form and immense strength.

5.9.s:
nirucchvāse nirucchvāsāstiṣṭhanti narake ciram |
uttāḍyante tathocchvāse vālukāsadane narāḥ ||
5.9.d:
निरुच्छ्वासे निरुच्छ्वासास्तिष्ठन्ति नरके चिरम् ।
उत्ताड्यन्ते तथोच्छ्वासे वालुकासदने नराः ॥
5.9.m: In [the hell] Nirucchvāsa, men remain for a long time breathless; / and in Ucchvāsa, they are severely beaten in the abode of sand.

5.9.s:
raurave rodamānāśca pīḍyante vividhairvadhaiḥ |
mahārauravapīḍābhirmahānto'pi rudanti ca ||
5.9.d:
रौरवे रोदमानाश्च पीड्यन्ते विविधैर्वधैः ।
महारौरवपीडाभिर्महान्तोऽपि रुदन्ति च ॥
5.9.m: In Raurava, weeping, they are tormented by various executions; / and through the torments of Mahāraurava, even the great weep.

5.9.s:
patsu vaktre gude muṇḍe netrayoścaiva mastake |
nihanyante ghanaistīkṣṇaiḥ sutaptairlohaśaṅkubhiḥ ||
5.9.d:
पत्सु वक्त्रे गुदे मुण्डे नेत्रयोश्चैव मस्तके ।
निहन्यन्ते घनैस्तीक्ष्णैः सुतप्तैर्लोहशङ्कुभिः ॥
5.9.m: On the feet, face, anus, head, eyes, and crown of the head, / they are struck with heavy, sharp, intensely heated iron spikes.

5.9.s:
sutaptavālukāyāṃ tu prayojyante muhurmuhuḥ |
jantupaṅke bhṛśaṃ tapte kṣiptāḥ krandanti visvaram ||
5.9.d:
सुतप्तवालुकायां तु प्रयोज्यन्ते मुहुर्मुहुः ।
जन्तुपङ्के भृशं तप्ते क्षिप्ताः क्रन्दन्ति विस्वरम् ॥
5.9.m: They are repeatedly placed upon intensely heated sand; / cast into an intensely heated mire of creatures, they wail discordant cries.

5.9.s:
kumbhīpākeṣu pacyante taptataileṣu vai mune |
pāpinaḥ krūrakarmāṇo'sahyeṣu sarvathā punaḥ ||
5.9.d:
कुम्भीपाकेषु पच्यन्ते तप्ततैलेषु वै मुने ।
पापिनः क्रूरकर्माणोऽसह्येषु सर्वथा पुनः ॥
5.9.m: In Kumbhīpāka hells they are cooked in boiling oil, O sage— / the sinners of cruel deeds, in conditions utterly unbearable.

5.9.s:
lālābhakṣeṣu pāpāste pātyante duḥkhadeṣu vai |
nānāsthāneṣu ca tathā narakeṣu punaḥpunaḥ ||
5.9.d:
लालाभक्षेषु पापास्ते पात्यन्ते दुःखदेषु वै ।
नानास्थानेषु च तथा नरकेषु पुनःपुनः ॥
5.9.m: In Lālābhakṣa those sinners are cast down, into misery-giving places, / and likewise in various places throughout the hells again and again.

5.9.s:
sūcīmukhe mahākleśe narake pātyate naraḥ |
pāpī puṇyavihīnaśca tāḍyate yamakiṅkaraiḥ ||
5.9.d:
सूचीमुखे महाक्लेशे नरके पात्यते नरः ।
पापी पुण्यविहीनश्च ताड्यते यमकिङ्करैः ॥
5.9.m: Into the hell Sūcīmukha of great anguish the man is cast; / sinful and devoid of merit, he is beaten by Yama's servants.

5.9.s:
lohakumbhe viniḥkṣiptāḥ śvasantaśca śanaiḥ śanaiḥ |
mahāgninā prapacyante svapāpaireva mānavāḥ ||
5.9.d:
लोहकुम्भे विनिःक्षिप्ताः श्वसन्तश्च शनैः शनैः ।
महाग्निना प्रपच्यन्ते स्वपापैरेव मानवाः ॥
5.9.m: Cast into an iron pot, gasping for breath slowly, / men are thoroughly cooked by a great fire solely because of their own sins.

5.9.s:
dṛḍhaṃ rajjvādibhirbaddhvā prapīḍyante śilāsu ca |
kṣipyante cāndhakūpeṣu daśyante bhramarairbhṛśam ||
5.9.d:
दृढं रज्ज्वादिभिर्बद्ध्वा प्रपीड्यन्ते शिलासु च ।
क्षिप्यन्ते चान्धकूपेषु दश्यन्ते भ्रमरैर्भृशम् ॥
5.9.m: Bound firmly with ropes and the like, they are crushed upon stones; / and they are thrown into blind wells and severely stung by bees.

5.9.s:
kṛmibhirbhinnasarvāṅgāḥ śataśo jarjarīkṛtāḥ |
sutīkṣṇakṣārakūpeṣu kṣipyante tadanantaram ||
5.9.d:
कृमिभिर्भिन्नसर्वाङ्गाः शतशो जर्जरीकृताः ।
सुतीक्ष्णक्षारकूपेषु क्षिप्यन्ते तदनन्तरम् ॥
5.9.m: With all their limbs pierced by worms, shattered into hundreds of pieces, / they are immediately thereafter thrown into wells of exceedingly sharp caustic.

5.9.s:
mahājvāle'tra narake pāpāḥ krandanti duḥkhitāḥ |
itaścetaśca dhāvanti dahyamānāstadarciṣā ||
5.9.d:
महाज्वालेऽत्र नरके पापाः क्रन्दन्ति दुःखिताः ।
इतश्चेतश्च धावन्ति दह्यमानास्तदर्चिषा ॥
5.9.m: In this hell Mahājvāla, the suffering sinners scream; / they run hither and thither, burning in its flames.

5.9.s:
pṛṣṭhe cānīya tuṇḍābhyāṃ vinyastaskandhayojite |
tayormadhyena vākṛṣya bāhupṛṣṭhena gāḍhataḥ ||
5.9.d:
पृष्ठे चानीय तुण्डाभ्यां विन्यस्तस्कन्धयोजिते ।
तयोर्मध्येन वाकृष्य बाहुपृष्ठेन गाढतः ॥
5.9.m: Brought onto the back by two beaks, fixed onto the shoulders joined together, / or pulled through the middle of the two, tightly behind the arms,

5.9.s:
baddhāḥ parasparaṃ sarve subhṛśaṃ pāśarajjubhiḥ |
baddhapiṇḍāstu dṛśyante mahājvāle tu yātanāḥ ||
5.9.d:
बद्धाः परस्परं सर्वे सुभृशं पाशरज्जुभिः ।
बद्धपिण्डास्तु दृश्यन्ते महाज्वाले तु यातनाः ॥
5.9.m: all tied firmly to one another with ropes of fetters, / they are seen as bound masses enduring torments in Mahājvāla.

5.9.s:
rajjubhirveṣṭitāścaiva praliptāḥ kardamena ca |
karīṣatuṣavahnau ca pacyante na mriyanti ca ||
5.9.d:
रज्जुभिर्वेष्टिताश्चैव प्रलिप्ताः कर्दमेन च ।
करीषतुषवह्नौ च पच्यन्ते न म्रियन्ति च ॥
5.9.m: Encircled with ropes and smeared with mud, / they are cooked in a fire of dry cow-dung and chaff, yet they do not die.

5.9.s:
sutīkṣṇacaritāste hi karkaśāsu śilāsu ca |
āsphālya śataśaḥ pāpāḥ pacyante tṛṇavattataḥ ||
5.9.d:
सुतीक्ष्णचरितास्ते हि कर्कशासु शिलासु च ।
आस्फाल्य शतशः पापाः पच्यन्ते तृणवत्ततः ॥
5.9.m: Those of extremely harsh conduct, dashed hundreds of times / against rough stones, are then burned like grass, the sinners.

5.9.s:
śarīrābhyantaragataiḥ prabhūtaiḥ kṛmibhirnarāḥ |
bhakṣyante tīkṣṇavadanairātmadehakṣayād bhṛśam ||
5.9.d:
शरीराभ्यन्तरगतैः प्रभूतैः कृमिभिर्नराः ।
भक्ष्यन्ते तीक्ष्णवदनैरात्मदेहक्षयाद् भृशम् ॥
5.9.m: By abundant worms that have entered within their bodies, / men are eaten by the sharp-mouthed creatures severely, until the destruction of their own bodies.

5.9.s:
kṛmīṇāṃ nicaye kṣiptāḥ pūyamāṃsāsthirāśiṣu |
tiṣṭhantyudvignahṛdayāḥ parvatābhyāṃ nipīḍitāḥ ||
5.9.d:
कृमीणां निचये क्षिप्ताः पूयमांसास्थिराशिषु ।
तिष्ठन्त्युद्विग्नहृदयाः पर्वताभ्यां निपीडिताः ॥
5.9.m: Thrown into a multitude of worms, on heaps of pus, flesh, and bones, / they remain with anxious hearts, crushed between two mountains.

5.9.s:
taptena vajralepena śarīramanulipyate |
adhomukhordhvapādaśca tātapyante sma vahninā ||
5.9.d:
तप्तेन वज्रलेपेन शरीरमनुलिप्यते ।
अधोमुखोर्ध्वपादश्च तातप्यन्ते स्म वह्निना ॥
5.9.m: The body is smeared with heated diamond-hard plaster; / head downward and feet upward, they are scorched by fire.

5.9.s:
vadanāntaḥpravinyastāṃ suprataptāmayogadām |
te khādanti parādhīnāstaistāḍyante ca mudgaraiḥ ||
5.9.d:
वदनान्तःप्रविन्यस्तां सुप्रतप्तामयोगदाम् ।
ते खादन्ति पराधीनास्तैस्ताड्यन्ते च मुद्गरैः ॥
5.9.m: An intensely heated iron club placed within their mouth, / they eat it, helpless, and are beaten by them with mallets.

5.9.s:
itthaṃ vyāsa kukarmāṇo narakeṣu pacanti hi |
varṇayāmi vivarṇatvaṃ teṣāṃ tattvāya karmiṇām ||
śrīgaṇeśāya namaḥ ||
śrīgaurīśaṅkarābhyāṃ namaḥ ||
śrīśivamahāpurāṇam ||
5.9.d:
इत्थं व्यास कुकर्माणो नरकेषु पचन्ति हि ।
वर्णयामि विवर्णत्वं तेषां तत्त्वाय कर्मिणाम् ॥
श्रीगणेशाय नमः ॥
श्रीगौरीशङ्कराभ्यां नमः ॥
श्रीशिवमहापुराणम् ॥
5.9.m:
Thus, O Vyāsa, evil-doers are cooked in the hells; / I shall describe the loss of complexion of those perpetrators of deeds, for the sake of truth.

Obeisance to the glorious Gaurī and Śaṅkara.

5.10.s:
sanatkumāra uvāca |
mithyāgamaṃ pravṛttastu dvijihvākhyaṃ ca gacchati |
jihvārdhakośavistīrṇahalaistīkṣṇaiḥ prapīḍyate ||
5.10.d:
सनत्कुमार उवाच ।
मिथ्यागमं प्रवृत्तस्तु द्विजिह्वाख्यं च गच्छति ।
जिह्वार्धकोशविस्तीर्णहलैस्तीक्ष्णैः प्रपीड्यते ॥
5.10.m: Sanatkumāra said: / One who engages in false tradition goes to [the hell] named Dvijihva; / he is tormented by sharp plows wide as half a kośa of the tongue.

5.10.s:
nirbhartsayati yaḥ krūro mātaraṃ pitaraṃ gurum |
viṣṭhābhiḥ kṛmimiśrābhirmukhamāpūrya hanyate ||
5.10.d:
निर्भर्त्सयति यः क्रूरो मातरं पितरं गुरुम् ।
विष्ठाभिः कृमिमिश्राभिर्मुखमापूर्य हन्यते ॥
5.10.m: The cruel one who insults mother, father, or teacher, / his mouth is stuffed with feces mixed with worms, and he is beaten.

5.10.s:
ye śivāyatanārāmavāpīkūpataḍāgakān |
vidravanti dvijasthānaṃ narāstatra ramanti ca ||
5.10.d:
ये शिवायतनारामवापीकूपतडागकान् ।
विद्रवन्ति द्विजस्थानं नरास्तत्र रमन्ति च ॥
5.10.m: Those men who invade Śiva temples, pleasure gardens, stepwells, wells, / and reservoirs, or the dwelling of a twice-born, and sport there,

5.10.s:
kāmāyodvartanābhyaṅga snānapānāmbubhojanam |
krīḍanaṃ maithunaṃ dyūtamācaranti madoddhatāḥ ||
5.10.d:
कामायोद्वर्तनाभ्यङ्ग स्नानपानाम्बुभोजनम् ।
क्रीडनं मैथुनं द्यूतमाचरन्ति मदोद्धताः ॥
5.10.m: and, arrogant with pride, practice unction, massage, bathing, / drinking water, eating, sport, sexual intercourse, and gambling for sensual pleasure,

5.10.s:
pecire vividhairdhorairikṣuyantrādipīḍanaiḥ |
nirayāgniṣu pacyante yāvadābhūtasamplavam ||
5.10.d:
पेचिरे विविधैर्धोरैरिक्षुयन्त्रादिपीडनैः ।
निरयाग्निषु पच्यन्ते यावदाभूतसम्प्लवम् ॥
5.10.m: are cooked by various dreadful tortures, such as being crushed in sugarcane presses; / they are cooked in the fires of hell until the dissolution of all beings.

5.10.s:
tena tenaiva rūpeṇa tāḍyante pāradārikāḥ |
gāḍhamāliṅgya te nārīṃ sutaptāṃ lohanirmitām ||
5.10.d:
तेन तेनैव रूपेण ताड्यन्ते पारदारिकाः ।
गाढमालिङ्ग्य ते नारीं सुतप्तां लोहनिर्मिताम् ॥
5.10.m: Adulterers are beaten in that very manner; / having tightly embraced a woman made of red-hot iron,

5.10.s:
pūrvākārāśca puruṣāḥ prajvalanti samantataḥ |
duścāriṇīṃ striyaṃ gāḍhamāliṅganti rudanti ca ||
5.10.d:
पूर्वाकाराश्च पुरुषाः प्रज्वलन्ति समन्ततः ।
दुश्चारिणीं स्त्रियं गाढमालिङ्गन्ति रुदन्ति च ॥
5.10.m: men with their former forms burn on all sides; / they tightly embrace a woman of wicked conduct and weep.

5.10.s:
ye śṛṇvanti satāṃ nindāṃ teṣāṃ karṇaprapūraṇam |
agnivarṇairayaḥkīlaistaptaistāmrādinirmitaiḥ ||
5.10.d:
ये शृण्वन्ति सतां निन्दां तेषां कर्णप्रपूरणम् ।
अग्निवर्णैरयःकीलैस्तप्तैस्ताम्रादिनिर्मितैः ॥
5.10.m: For those who listen to the slander of the virtuous, their ears are filled / with fire-colored iron spikes heated and made of copper and the like,

5.10.s:
trapusīsārakūṭādbhiḥ kṣīreṇa ca punaḥpunaḥ |
sutaptatīkṣṇatailena vajralepena vā punaḥ ||
5.10.d:
त्रपुसीसारकूटाद्भिः क्षीरेण च पुनःपुनः ।
सुतप्ततीक्ष्णतैलेन वज्रलेपेन वा पुनः ॥
5.10.m: with molten tin, lead, and brass, with boiling milk again and again, / with intensely heated, sharp oil, or with diamond-hard plaster.

5.10.s:
kramādāpūrya karṇāṃstu narakeṣu ca yātanāḥ |
anukrameṇa sarveṣu bhavantyetāḥ samantataḥ ||
5.10.d:
क्रमादापूर्य कर्णांस्तु नरकेषु च यातनाः ।
अनुक्रमेण सर्वेषु भवन्त्येताः समन्ततः ॥
5.10.m: Filling their ears in order, the torments in hells / follow in succession throughout all of them on all sides.

5.10.s:
sarvendriyāṇāmapyevaṃ kramātpāpena yātanāḥ |
bhavanti ghorāḥ pratyekaṃ śarīreṇa kṛtena ca ||
5.10.d:
सर्वेन्द्रियाणामप्येवं क्रमात्पापेन यातनाः ।
भवन्ति घोराः प्रत्येकं शरीरेण कृतेन च ॥
5.10.m: So too, in order of the sin committed with each of all the senses, / terrible torments arise individually for each deed done by the body.

5.10.s:
sparśadoṣeṇa ye mūḍhāḥ spṛśanti ca parastriyam |
teṣāṃ karo'gnivarṇābhiḥ pāṃsubhiḥ pūryate bhṛśam ||
5.10.d:
स्पर्शदोषेण ये मूढाः स्पृशन्ति च परस्त्रियम् ।
तेषां करोऽग्निवर्णाभिः पांसुभिः पूर्यते भृशम् ॥
5.10.m: The fools who, through the sin of touch, touch another's wife, / their hand is filled deeply with fiery embers and dust.

5.10.s:
teṣāṃ kṣārādibhiḥ sarvaiḥ śarīramanulipyate |
yātanāśca mahākaṣṭāḥ sarveṣu narakeṣu ca ||
5.10.d:
तेषां क्षारादिभिः सर्वैः शरीरमनुलिप्यते ।
यातनाश्च महाकष्टाः सर्वेषु नरकेषु च ॥
5.10.m: Their body is smeared completely with caustic liquids and the like, / and there are great, agonizing torments in all the hells.

5.10.s:
kurvanti pitrorbhṛkuṭiṃ karanetrāṇi ye narāḥ |
vaktrāṇi teṣāṃ sāntāni kīryante śaṅkubhirdṛḍham ||
5.10.d:
कुर्वन्ति पित्रोर्भृकुटिं करनेत्राणि ये नराः ।
वक्त्राणि तेषां सान्तानि कीर्यन्ते शङ्कुभिर्दृढम् ॥
5.10.m: Men who knit their brows, or make [threatening] hands, eyes, / and mouths at their parents have them completely pierced through with spikes.

5.10.s:
yairindriyairnarā ye ca vikurvanti parastriyam |
indriyāṇi ca teṣāṃ vai vikurvanti tathaiva ca ||
5.10.d:
यैरिन्द्रियैर्नरा ये च विकुर्वन्ति परस्त्रियम् ।
इन्द्रियाणि च तेषां वै विकुर्वन्ति तथैव च ॥
5.10.m: Whatever sense organs men use to violate another's wife, / those very sense organs of theirs are mutilated accordingly.

5.10.s:
paradārāṃśca paśyanti lubdhāḥ stabdhena cakṣuṣā |
sūcībhiścāgnivarṇābhisteṣāṃ netraprapūraṇam ||
5.10.d:
परदारांश्च पश्यन्ति लुब्धाः स्तब्धेन चक्षुषा ।
सूचीभिश्चाग्निवर्णाभिस्तेषां नेत्रप्रपूरणम् ॥
5.10.m: Greedy men who gaze at another's wife with unblinking eyes, / their eyes are filled with fire-colored needles.

5.10.s:
kṣārādyaiśca kramātsarvā ihaiva yamayātanāḥ |
bhavanti muniśārdūla satyaṃ satyaṃ na saṃśayaḥ ||
5.10.d:
क्षाराद्यैश्च क्रमात्सर्वा इहैव यमयातनाः ।
भवन्ति मुनिशार्दूल सत्यं सत्यं न संशयः ॥
5.10.m: By caustic liquids and the like, all these torments of Yama / take place in order right here, O tiger among sages; it is true, true, there is no doubt.

5.10.s:
devāgniguruviprebhyaścānivedya prabhuñjate |
lohakīlaśataistaptaistajjihvāsyaṃ ca pūryate ||
5.10.d:
देवाग्निगुरुविप्रेभ्यश्चानिवेद्य प्रभुञ्जते ।
लोहकीलशतैस्तप्तैस्तज्जिह्वास्यं च पूर्यते ॥
5.10.m: Those who eat without offering to the gods, fire, guru, and brahmins, / their mouth and tongue are pierced with hundreds of heated iron nails.

5.10.s:
ye devārāmapuṣpāṇi lobhātsaṅgṛhya pāṇinā |
jighranti ca narā bhūyaḥ śirasā dhārayanti ca ||
5.10.d:
ये देवारामपुष्पाणि लोभात्सङ्गृह्य पाणिना ।
जिघ्रन्ति च नरा भूयः शिरसा धारयन्ति च ॥
5.10.m: Those men who, seizing them with their hand out of greed, / smell flowers from temple gardens, and wear them on their head,

5.10.s:
āpūryate śirasteṣāṃ taptairlohasya śaṅkubhiḥ |
nāsikā cātibahulaistataḥ kṣārādibhirbhṛśam ||
5.10.d:
आपूर्यते शिरस्तेषां तप्तैर्लोहस्य शङ्कुभिः ।
नासिका चातिबहुलैस्ततः क्षारादिभिर्भृशम् ॥
5.10.m: their head is filled with heated iron spikes, / their nose intensely with many [spikes], and then heavily with caustic liquids and the like.

5.10.s:
ye nindanti mahātmānaṃ vācakaṃ dharmadeśikam |
devāgnigurubhaktāṃśca dharmaśāstraṃ ca śāśvatam ||
5.10.d:
ये निन्दन्ति महात्मानं वाचकं धर्मदेशिकम् ।
देवाग्निगुरुभक्तांश्च धर्मशास्त्रं च शाश्वतम् ॥
5.10.m: Those who revile a noble reciter, a teacher of dharma, / devotees of gods, fire, and guru, and the eternal scripture of dharma,

5.10.s:
teṣāmurasi kaṇṭhe ca jihvāyāṃ dantasandhiṣu |
tālunyoṣṭhe nāsikāyāṃ mūrdhni sarvāṅgasandhiṣu ||
5.10.d:
तेषामुरसि कण्ठे च जिह्वायां दन्तसन्धिषु ।
तालुन्योष्ठे नासिकायां मूर्ध्नि सर्वाङ्गसन्धिषु ॥
5.10.m: in their chest, throat, tongue, joints of the teeth, / palate, lips, nose, head, and all the joints of their limbs,

5.10.s:
agnivarṇāstu taptāśca triśākhā lohaśaṅkavaḥ |
ākhidyante ca bahuśaḥ sthāneṣveteṣu mudgaraiḥ ||
5.10.d:
अग्निवर्णास्तु तप्ताश्च त्रिशाखा लोहशङ्कवः ।
आखिद्यन्ते च बहुशः स्थानेष्वेतेषु मुद्गरैः ॥
5.10.m: red-hot, fire-colored, three-pronged iron spikes / are repeatedly driven into these places with mallets.

5.10.s:
tataḥ kṣāreṇa dīptena pūryate hi samantataḥ |
yātanāśca mahatyo vai śarīrasyāti sarvataḥ ||
5.10.d:
ततः क्षारेण दीप्तेन पूर्यते हि समन्ततः ।
यातनाश्च महत्यो वै शरीरस्याति सर्वतः ॥
5.10.m: Then indeed it is filled on all sides with burning caustic liquid, / and there are great torments exceedingly everywhere upon the body.

5.10.s:
aśeṣanarakeṣveva kramanti kramaśaḥ punaḥ |
ye gṛhṇanti paradravyaṃ padbhyāṃ vipraṃ spṛśanti ca ||
5.10.d:
अशेषनरकेष्वेव क्रमन्ति क्रमशः पुनः ।
ये गृह्णन्ति परद्रव्यं पद्भ्यां विप्रं स्पृशन्ति च ॥
5.10.m: They proceed through all the hells successively again and again. / Those who take another's property and touch a brahmin with their feet,

5.10.s:
śivopakaraṇaṃ gāṃ ca jñānādilikhitaṃ ca yat |
hastapādādibhisteṣāmāpūryante samantataḥ ||
5.10.d:
शिवोपकरणं गां च ज्ञानादिलिखितं च यत् ।
हस्तपादादिभिस्तेषामापूर्यन्ते समन्ततः ॥
5.10.m: or [touch] an implement of Śiva, a cow, or what is written of spiritual knowledge and the like, / are pierced on all sides in their hands, feet, and other limbs.

5.10.s:
narakeṣu ca sarveṣu vicitrā bahuyātanāḥ |
bhavanti bahuśaḥ kaṣṭāḥ pāṇipādasamudbhavāḥ ||
5.10.d:
नरकेषु च सर्वेषु विचित्रा बहुयातनाः ।
भवन्ति बहुशः कष्टाः पाणिपादसमुद्भवाः ॥
5.10.m: And throughout all the hells there are diverse, manifold torments, / arising many times with great anguish on account of the hands and feet.

5.10.s:
śivāyatanaparyante devārāmeṣu kutracit |
samutsṛjanti ye pāpāḥ purīṣaṃ mūtrameva ca ||
5.10.d:
शिवायतनपर्यन्ते देवारामेषु कुत्रचित् ।
समुत्सृजन्ति ये पापाः पुरीषं मूत्रमेव च ॥
5.10.m: The sinners who, around the precincts of a Śiva shrine / or in temple gardens anywhere, discharge feces or urine,

5.10.s:
teṣāṃ śiśnaṃ savṛṣaṇaṃ cūrṇyate lohamudgaraiḥ |
sūcībhiragnivarṇābhistathā tvāpūryate punaḥ ||
5.10.d:
तेषां शिश्नं सवृषणं चूर्ण्यते लोहमुद्गरैः ।
सूचीभिरग्निवर्णाभिस्तथा त्वापूर्यते पुनः ॥
5.10.m: their penis and testicles are crushed with iron mallets, / and then pierced through again with fire-colored needles.

5.10.s:
tataḥ kṣāreṇa mahatā tīvreṇa ca punaḥ punaḥ |
drutena pūryate gāḍhaṃ gude śiśne ca dehinaḥ ||
5.10.d:
ततः क्षारेण महता तीव्रेण च पुनः पुनः ।
द्रुतेन पूर्यते गाढं गुदे शिश्ने च देहिनः ॥
5.10.m: Then, with molten, intense, and abundant caustic fluid, / the anus and penis of the embodied soul are repeatedly filled deep.

5.10.s:
manaḥ sarvendriyāṇāṃ ca yasmādduḥkhaṃ prajāyate |
dhane satyapi ye dānaṃ na prayacchanti tṛṣṇayā ||
5.10.d:
मनः सर्वेन्द्रियाणां च यस्माद्दुःखं प्रजायते ।
धने सत्यपि ये दानं न प्रयच्छन्ति तृष्णया ॥
5.10.m: From which suffering arises for the mind and all the sense organs. / Those who, even when wealth is at hand, do not give gifts out of greed,

5.10.s:
atithiṃ cāvamanyante kāle prāpte gṛhāśrame |
tasmātte duṣkṛtaṃ prāpya gacchanti niraye'śucau ||
5.10.d:
अतिथिं चावमन्यन्ते काले प्राप्ते गृहाश्रमे ।
तस्मात्ते दुष्कृतं प्राप्य गच्छन्ति निरयेऽशुचौ ॥
5.10.m: and disrespect a guest who arrives in due time at the householder's stage of life, / they, reaping evil deeds, go to an impure hell.

5.10.s:
ye'nnaṃ dattvā hi bhuñjanti na śvabhyaḥ saha vāyasaiḥ |
teṣāṃ ca vivṛtaṃ vaktraṃ kīlakadvayatāḍitam ||
5.10.d:
येऽन्नं दत्त्वा हि भुञ्जन्ति न श्वभ्यः सह वायसैः ।
तेषां च विवृतं वक्त्रं कीलकद्वयताडितम् ॥
5.10.m: Those who eat food without having given to the dogs along with the crows, / their mouth is forced open and pierced with two pegs;

5.10.s:
kṛmibhiḥ prāṇibhiścograirlohatuṇḍaiśca vāyasaiḥ |
upadravairbahuvidhairugrairantaḥ prapīḍyate ||
5.10.d:
कृमिभिः प्राणिभिश्चोग्रैर्लोहतुण्डैश्च वायसैः ।
उपद्रवैर्बहुविधैरुग्रैरन्तः प्रपीड्यते ॥
5.10.m: and inside they are fiercely tormented by worms, by ferocious creatures, / by crows with iron beaks, and by diverse, severe afflictions.

5.10.s:
śyāmaśca śabalaścaiva yamamārgānurodhakau |
yau stastābhyāṃ prayacchāmi tau gṛhṇītāmimaṃ balim ||
5.10.d:
श्यामश्च शबलश्चैव यममार्गानुरोधकौ ।
यौ स्तस्ताभ्यां प्रयच्छामि तौ गृह्णीतामिमं बलिम् ॥
5.10.m: 'Śyāma and Śabala, who block the path of Yama: / to you two who are present I offer; may you two accept this oblation.'

5.10.s:
ye vā varuṇavāyavyā yāmyā nairṛtyavāyasāḥ |
vāyasāḥ puṇyakarmāṇaste pragṛhṇantu me balim ||
5.10.d:
ये वा वरुणवायव्या याम्या नैरृत्यवायसाः ।
वायसाः पुण्यकर्माणस्ते प्रगृह्णन्तु मे बलिम् ॥
5.10.m: 'Or those crows of the western, northwestern, southern, and southwestern quarters, / crows of meritorious deeds: may they take my oblation.'

5.10.s:
śivāmabhyarcya yatnena hutvāgnau vidhipūrvakam |
śaivairmantrairbaliṃ ye ca dadante na ca te yamam ||
5.10.d:
शिवामभ्यर्च्य यत्नेन हुत्वाग्नौ विधिपूर्वकम् ।
शैवैर्मन्त्रैर्बलिं ये च ददन्ते न च ते यमम् ॥
5.10.m: Having carefully worshiped Śivā and offered into the fire according to rule, / those who offer the bali oblation with Śaiva mantras do not see Yama;

5.10.s:
paśyanti tridivaṃ yānti tasmāddadyāddinedine |
maṇḍalaṃ caturasraṃ tu kṛtvā gandhādivāsitam ||
5.10.d:
पश्यन्ति त्रिदिवं यान्ति तस्माद्दद्याद्दिनेदिने ।
मण्डलं चतुरस्रं तु कृत्वा गन्धादिवासितम् ॥
5.10.m: they go to heaven. Therefore one should offer it day by day. / Having drawn a four-cornered diagram and perfumed it with fragrances and the like,

5.10.s:
dhanvantaryarthamīśānyāṃ prācyāmindrāya niḥkṣipet |
yāmyāṃ yamāya vāruṇyāṃ sudakṣomāya dakṣiṇe ||
5.10.d:
धन्वन्तर्यर्थमीशान्यां प्राच्यामिन्द्राय निःक्षिपेत् ।
याम्यां यमाय वारुण्यां सुदक्षोमाय दक्षिणे ॥
5.10.m: one should place [an offering] for Dhanvantari in the northeast, for Indra in the east, / for Yama in the south, for Varuṇa in the west, and for Soma in the north.

5.10.s:
pitṛbhyastu viniḥkṣipya prācyāmaryamaṇaṃ tataḥ |
dhātuścaiva vidhātuśca dvāradeśe viniḥkṣipet ||
5.10.d:
पितृभ्यस्तु विनिःक्षिप्य प्राच्यामर्यमणं ततः ।
धातुश्चैव विधातुश्च द्वारदेशे विनिःक्षिपेत् ॥
5.10.m: Then, after placing [an offering] for the ancestors, one should place [one] for Aryaman in the east, / and one should place [offerings] for Dhātṛ and Vidhātṛ at the entrance.

5.10.s:
śvabhyaśca śvapatibhyaśca vayobhyo vikṣipedbhuvi |
devaiḥ pitṛmanuṣyaiśca pretairbhūtaiḥ saguhyakaiḥ ||
5.10.d:
श्वभ्यश्च श्वपतिभ्यश्च वयोभ्यो विक्षिपेद्भुवि ।
देवैः पितृमनुष्यैश्च प्रेतैर्भूतैः सगुह्यकैः ॥
5.10.m: One should scatter [offerings] on the ground for dogs, dog-masters, and birds. / By gods, ancestors, men, ghosts, beings along with Guhyakas,

5.10.s:
vayobhiḥ kṛmikīṭaiśca gṛhasthaścopajīvyate |
svāhākāraḥ svadhākāro vaṣaṭkārastṛtīyakaḥ ||
5.10.d:
वयोभिः कृमिकीटैश्च गृहस्थश्चोपजीव्यते ।
स्वाहाकारः स्वधाकारो वषट्कारस्तृतीयकः ॥
5.10.m: birds, worms, and insects, the householder is lived upon [for sustenance]. / Svāhākāra, svadhākāra, and vaṣaṭkāra as the third,

5.10.s:
hantakārastathaivānyo dhenvāḥ stanacatuṣṭayam |
svāhākāraṃ stanaṃ devāḥ svadhāṃ ca pitarastathā ||
5.10.d:
हन्तकारस्तथैवान्यो धेन्वाः स्तनचतुष्टयम् ।
स्वाहाकारं स्तनं देवाः स्वधां च पितरस्तथा ॥
5.10.m: and hantakāra as the other, are the four teats of the cow. / The gods drink from the teat that is svāhākāra, and the ancestors from svadhā;

5.10.s:
vaṣaṭkāraṃ tathaivānye devā bhūteśvarāstathā |
hantakāraṃ manuṣyāśca pibanti satataṃ stanam ||
5.10.d:
वषट्कारं तथैवान्ये देवा भूतेश्वरास्तथा ।
हन्तकारं मनुष्याश्च पिबन्ति सततं स्तनम् ॥
5.10.m: likewise the other gods and lords of beings drink from vaṣaṭkāra, / and men constantly drink from the teat that is hantakāra.

5.10.s:
yastvetāṃ mānavo dhenuṃ śraddhayā hyanupūrvikām |
karoti satataṃ kāle sāgnitvāyopakalpyate ||
5.10.d:
यस्त्वेतां मानवो धेनुं श्रद्धया ह्यनुपूर्विकाम् ।
करोति सततं काले साग्नित्वायोपकल्प्यते ॥
5.10.m: Whatever mortal faithfully and continuously keeps this cow in due order / at the proper time, it is regarded as having maintained the sacred fires.

5.10.s:
yastāṃ jahāti vāsvasthastāmisre sa tu majjati |
tasmāddattvā baliṃ tebhyo dvārasthaścintayetkṣaṇam ||
5.10.d:
यस्तां जहाति वास्वस्थस्तामिस्रे स तु मज्जति ।
तस्माद्दत्त्वा बलिं तेभ्यो द्वारस्थश्चिन्तयेत्क्षणम् ॥
5.10.m: He who abandons it while able sinks into Tāmisra hell. / Therefore, having offered oblation to them, standing at the door one should reflect for a moment.

5.10.s:
kṣudhārtamatithiṃ samyagekagrāmanivāsinam |
bhojayettaṃ śubhānnena yathāśaktyātmabhojanāt ||
5.10.d:
क्षुधार्तमतिथिं सम्यगेकग्रामनिवासिनम् ।
भोजयेत्तं शुभान्नेन यथाशक्त्यात्मभोजनात् ॥
5.10.m: One should properly feed a hungry guest, even one residing in the same village, / with wholesome food according to one's means, from one's own food.

5.10.s:
atithiryasya bhagnāśo gṛhātpratinivartate |
sa tasmai duṣkṛtaṃ dattvā puṇyamādāya gacchati ||
5.10.d:
अतिथिर्यस्य भग्नाशो गृहात्प्रतिनिवर्तते ।
स तस्मै दुष्कृतं दत्त्वा पुण्यमादाय गच्छति ॥
5.10.m: The guest who turns back from one's house with his hopes broken / gives him his own misdeeds, takes his merit, and departs.

5.10.s:
tato'nnaṃ priyamevāśnannaraḥ śṛṅkhalavān punaḥ |
jihvāvegena viddho'tra ciraṃ kālaṃ sa tiṣṭhati ||
5.10.d:
ततोऽन्नं प्रियमेवाश्नन्नरः शृङ्खलवान् पुनः ।
जिह्वावेगेन विद्धोऽत्र चिरं कालं स तिष्ठति ॥
5.10.m: Afterwards, that man who merely eats delicious food is put in chains; / pierced here by the impetus of his tongue, he stays for a long time.

5.10.s:
yatastammāṃsamuddhṛtya tilamātrapramāṇataḥ |
khādituṃ dīyate teṣāṃ bhittvā caiva tu śoṇitam ||
5.10.d:
यतस्तम्मांसमुद्धृत्य तिलमात्रप्रमाणतः ।
खादितुं दीयते तेषां भित्त्वा चैव तु शोणितम् ॥
5.10.m: Whereupon, cutting his flesh in sizes measuring only a sesame seed, / it is given to them to eat, and his blood is pierced and drawn.

5.10.s:
niḥśeṣataḥ kaśābhistu pīḍyate kramaśaḥ punaḥ |
bubhukṣayātikaṣṭaṃ hi tathācātipipāsayā ||
5.10.d:
